translations.literal: The next day news arrived that Ming Rui had fallen in battle; E'ning impeached Wu'erdenge for deliberate negligence and delay; an edict ordered him seized and brought to the capital and dismembered, and Tan Wuge was also executed in the marketplace, while Ming Rui was generously compensated.
translations.idiomatic: The next day came word that Ming Rui had fallen in battle; E'ning impeached Wu'erdenge for deliberate delay and negligence; an edict ordered him brought to the capital and dismembered, Tan Wuge was executed in the marketplace, and Ming Rui's family was generously compensated.

sentences.zh: 其後阿裏袞募人至猛育，求其屍，歸於京師以葬。

translations.literal: Afterward Arigun recruited men to go to Mengyu, recovered his body, and brought it to the capital for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Later Arigun hired men to go to Mengyu, recover Ming Rui's body, and bring it to the capital for burial.

sentences.zh: 是為征緬前一役。

translations.literal: This was the first Burma campaign.
translations.idiomatic: This concluded the first Burma expedition.

sentences.zh: 明瑞之死也，緬人不知，震其餘威，懼再討。

translations.literal: When Ming Rui died, the Burmese did not know; they feared his lingering prestige and dreaded another punitive expedition.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese did not yet know of Ming Rui's death; they still feared his reputation and dreaded another Qing invasion.

sentences.zh: 五月，縱所獲兵許爾功等八人自木邦持緬書來，且使楊重英、王呈瑞等言：「懵駁之母得罪天朝，欲使懵駁內附。」

translations.literal: In the fifth month, they released eight captured soldiers including Xu Ergong from Mohnyin with a Burmese letter, and sent Yang Chongying, Wang Chengrui, and others to say: "Mengbo's mother has offended the Celestial Court; she wishes Mengbo to submit to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Burma released eight captured soldiers, including Xu Ergong, from Mohnyin with a Burmese letter, and sent Yang Chongying, Wang Chengrui, and others to say: "Mengbo's mother has offended the Celestial Court and wishes Mengbo to submit to the Qing.

sentences.zh: 重英恐緬書繙譯誤，乃譯清、漢字各一通，益以木邦臘戌頭目苗溫之書。

translations.literal: Yang Chongying feared errors in translating the Burmese letter, so he prepared one copy each in Manchu and Chinese characters, and added a letter from Mohnyin lapsha chieftain Miao Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing mistranslation of the Burmese letter, Yang Chongying prepared separate Manchu and Chinese versions and added a letter from Miao Wen, the lapsha chieftain of Mohnyin.

sentences.zh: 苗溫者，緬人守土官之稱。

translations.literal: Miao Wen was the Burmese title for a local territorial official.
translations.idiomatic: Miao Wen held the Burmese title for a local territorial official.

sentences.zh: 臘戌在木邦南。

translations.literal: Lapsha lay south of Mohnyin.
translations.idiomatic: Lapsha stood south of Mohnyin.

sentences.zh: 木邦殘破，而臘戍城在嶺下，險可守，故苗溫徙居於此。

translations.literal: Mohnyin was ravaged, but Lapsha city stood below a ridge, defensible by terrain, so Miao Wen moved there.
translations.idiomatic: Mohnyin lay in ruins, but Lapsha city below the ridge was easily defended, so Miao Wen had moved there.

sentences.zh: 緬書云：「暹羅國、得楞國、得懷國、白古國、一勘國、罕紀國、結㱔國、大耳國及金銀寶石廠，飛刀、飛馬、飛人、有福好善之王殿下掌事官拜書領兵元帥。

translations.literal: The Burmese letter read: "To the kingdoms of Siam, Tenasserim, Thaton, Pegu, Kyaukse, Hanthawaddy, Kengtung, and the Big-Ear country, and the gold, silver, and gem mines—the Flying Knife, Flying Horse, Flying Man, fortunate and benevolent king's ministerial officer writes in salutation, commander-in-chief of troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese letter opened: "To the kingdoms of Siam, Tenasserim, Thaton, Pegu, Kyaukse, Hanthawaddy, Kengtung, and the Big-Ear country, and the gold, silver, and gem mines—the Flying Knife, Flying Horse, Flying Man, fortunate and benevolent king's minister writes in salutation, commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 昔吳尚賢至阿瓦，敬述大皇帝仁慈樂善，我緬王用是具禮致貢，蒙賜緞帛、玉器諸物，自是商旅相通，初無仇隙。

translations.literal: Formerly Wu Shangxian came to Ava and respectfully described the Great Emperor's benevolence and love of charity; our Burmese king accordingly offered tribute with full ceremony and received gifts of silk, jade, and other objects; since then merchants traveled back and forth and there was originally no enmity.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Wu Shangxian came to Ava and praised the Great Emperor's benevolence; our king thereupon sent tribute with full ceremony and received silk, jade, and other gifts; since then merchants traveled freely and there was no enmity between us.

sentences.zh: 近因木邦、蠻暮土司播弄是非，興兵兆釁，致彼此人馬互有傷亡。

translations.literal: Recently because Mohnyin and Mangmu chieftains stirred up trouble, troops were raised and conflict began, causing casualties on both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the Mohnyin and Mangmu chieftains stirred up trouble, provoking war and causing casualties on both sides.

sentences.zh: 茲特投文敘明顛末，請循古禮，貢賜往來，永息干戈，照舊和好。」

translations.literal: We now specially send this document explaining the whole course of events, requesting to follow ancient ritual, exchange tribute and gifts, permanently cease arms, and restore friendship as before."
translations.idiomatic: We now send this document explaining the whole affair, asking to restore the old tribute exchange, lay down arms forever, and renew friendship as before."

sentences.zh: 阿裏袞以聞。

translations.literal: Arigun reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Arigun reported the letter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝念明瑞軍入關者尚逾萬，所喪亡不過十之一二，然將帥親臣皆捐軀異域，而緬夷求款未親遣頭目，非大舉無以雪忠憤，命絕之勿報。

translations.literal: The emperor reflected that of Ming Rui's army that had crossed the pass, more than ten thousand remained, and losses were no more than one or two in ten—yet generals and personal ministers of the court had given their lives in a foreign land, while the Burmese sought peace without personally sending a chief; only a major campaign could satisfy loyal indignation; he ordered them rejected with no reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor noted that more than ten thousand of Ming Rui's men had crossed the pass and losses were only one or two in ten—yet his generals and close ministers had died in a foreign land, while the Burmese sued for peace without sending a chief in person; only a major campaign could satisfy loyal grief and anger, and he ordered the overture rejected without reply.

sentences.zh: 自後緬人數以書與隴正野人及遮放土司訪問許爾功狀，皆置不答；

translations.literal: Afterward the Burmese repeatedly sent letters to Longzheng wild tribesmen and the Zhefang chieftain inquiring after Xu Ergong's situation—all were left unanswered;
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the Burmese repeatedly sent letters through Longzheng tribesmen and the Zhefang chieftain asking after Xu Ergong—all went unanswered;

sentences.zh: 而以楊重英偷生阿瓦，籍其家，並置其子於理。

translations.literal: And because Yang Chongying had clung to life in Ava, his household property was confiscated and his son was put on trial.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Chongying had chosen to live on in Ava, his family property was confiscated and his son was brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 時大學士公傅恆自請督師，乃命為經略；

translations.literal: At this time Grand Secretary Duke Fu Heng volunteered to supervise the army, and he was appointed campaign commander-in-chief;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Duke Fu Heng then volunteered to take command and was appointed campaign commander-in-chief;

sentences.zh: 阿桂、阿裏袞皆為副將軍，明德為總督，哈國興為提督。

translations.literal: Agui and Arigun were both made deputy generals, Mingde governor-general, and Ha Guoxing military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Agui and Arigun were appointed deputy generals, Mingde governor-general, and Ha Guoxing military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 八月，阿桂詣熱河行在，奏言：「緬賊湣不畏死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Agui went to the imperial presence at Rehe and memorialized: "The Burmese rebels plainly do not fear death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Agui went to the emperor at Rehe and memorialized: "The Burmese rebels plainly do not fear death.

sentences.zh: 臣至滇，當相度時勢，以正天誅，不敢鹵莽滅裂，誤軍國大事。」

translations.literal: When your servant reaches Yunnan, I shall gauge the times and carry out Heaven's punishment; I dare not act rashly and ruinously and botch affairs of state and army."
translations.idiomatic: When I reach Yunnan I shall weigh the situation and carry out Heaven's punishment; I dare not act rashly and ruin the campaign."

sentences.zh: 帝頷之。

translations.literal: The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor nodded approval.

sentences.zh: 既陛辭，至襄陽，會守備程轍前從楊寧軍陷於賊，至是密以書來告，言緬人方與暹羅仇殺，可約以夾攻。

translations.literal: After taking leave at court, when he reached Xiangyang, Garrison Commander Cheng Zhe, who had previously been captured with Yang Ning's army by the rebels, now secretly sent a letter reporting that the Burmese were then at war with Siam and a joint attack could be arranged.
translations.idiomatic: After taking leave at court, Agui reached Xiangyang and received a secret letter from Garrison Commander Cheng Zhe, who had been captured with Yang Ning's army and reported that the Burmese were then fighting Siam and could be attacked from both sides.

sentences.zh: 帝遣人馳問阿桂，奏言：「官軍會合暹羅，必赴緬地。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched someone to inquire urgently of Agui, who memorialized: "If imperial troops join Siam, they must go to Burmese territory.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent an urgent inquiry to Agui, who replied: "If imperial troops were to join Siam, they would have to march into Burma.

sentences.zh: 若由廣東往，則遠隔重洋，相去萬餘里，期會在數月之後，恐不能如期。」

translations.literal: If they go from Guangdong, they would be separated by vast seas, more than ten thousand li apart; the rendezvous would be months away and might not be kept on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: If they went from Guangdong they would cross vast seas, more than ten thousand li apart; the rendezvous would fall months later and might not be kept."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 蓋自明陳用賓有要暹羅攻緬之說，楊應琚、楊廷璋先後奏上，延議雖斥之，不能釋然也。

translations.literal: For since the Ming official Chen Yongbin had proposed urging Siam to attack Burma, and Yang Yingju and Yang Tingzhang had successively memorialized it, although court debate had rejected it, the idea could not be dismissed from mind.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Ming official Chen Yongbin had proposed urging Siam to attack Burma, and Yang Yingju and Yang Tingzhang had revived the idea, court debate had rejected it—but the notion would not die.

sentences.zh: 因詔兩廣總督李侍堯詢察之。

translations.literal: An edict therefore ordered Guangdong-Guangxi Governor-General Li Shiyao to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: An edict therefore ordered Guangdong-Guangxi Governor-General Li Shiyao to investigate.

sentences.zh: 侍堯奏言：「聞暹羅為花肚番殘破，國主詔氏竄跡他所，餘地為屬下甘恩敕、莫士麟分據。」

translations.literal: Li Shiyao memorialized: "I hear Siam has been ravaged by the Huadufen; the royal Zhao house has fled elsewhere; the remaining territory is divided among subordinates Gan Endu and Mo Shilin."
translations.idiomatic: Li Shiyao reported: "I hear Siam has been ravaged by the Huadufen; the Zhao royal house has fled, and the remaining territory is divided between subordinates Gan Endu and Mo Shilin."

sentences.zh: 花肚番者，緬人以膝股為花，故云。

translations.literal: The Huadufen were so called because the Burmese tattooed flowers on their thighs and hips.
translations.idiomatic: The Huadufen were so called because the Burmese tattooed their thighs and hips with floral designs.

sentences.zh: 由是約暹羅之議始寢。

translations.literal: Thus the plan to ally with Siam was finally dropped.
translations.idiomatic: With that the plan to ally with Siam was dropped.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，帝念明瑞所統旗兵勞苦，命回京，復選旗兵五千人赴滇，合荊州、貴州、四川兵一萬三千人。

translations.literal: That winter the emperor, mindful of the hardship borne by the Banner troops Ming Rui had commanded, ordered them back to the capital and selected five thousand Banner soldiers for Yunnan, together with thirteen thousand troops from Jingzhou, Guizhou, and Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, mindful of the hardship borne by the Banner troops under Ming Rui, the emperor ordered them home and sent five thousand fresh Banner soldiers to Yunnan, together with thirteen thousand men from Jingzhou, Guizhou, and Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 阿裏袞乃令副都統綿康、曲尋鎮總兵常青帥二千人駐隴川，侍衛海蘭察、烏爾圖納遜帥二千人駐盞達，領隊大臣豐安、鶴麗鎮總兵德福帥二千人駐遮放，侍衛興兆、巴朗帥一千人駐芒市，侍衛玉林、普爾普帥五百人亦駐盞達，侍衛恆山保、永順鎮總兵常保柱帥三千人駐永昌，廣東右翼鎮總兵樊經文帥一千人駐緬甯，荊州將軍永瑞、四川副都統雅朗阿、提督五福帥六千人駐普洱，而騰越兵一千令綿康兼轄之。

translations.literal: Arigun then ordered Deputy Lieutenant-General Miankang and Qujing commander Changqing to lead two thousand men stationed at Longchuan; Bodyguards Hailancha and Wu'ertunaxun two thousand at Zanda; expedition minister Feng'an and Heqing commander Defu two thousand at Zhefang; Bodyguards Xingzhao and Balang one thousand at Mangshi; Bodyguards Yulin and Pu'erpu five hundred also at Zanda; Bodyguards Hengshanbao and Yongshun commander Chang Baozhu three thousand at Yongchang; Guangdong Right Wing commander Fan Jingwen one thousand at Dianning; Jingzhou General Yongrui, Sichuan Deputy Lieutenant-General Yalang'a, and Military Commissioner Wufu six thousand at Pu'er; and one thousand Tengyue troops placed under Miankang's additional command.
translations.idiomatic: Arigun deployed his forces: Miankang and Qujing Commander Changqing with two thousand men at Longchuan; Bodyguards Hailancha and Wu'ertunaxun with two thousand at Zanda; Expedition Minister Feng'an and Heqing Commander Defu with two thousand at Zhefang; Bodyguards Xingzhao and Balang with one thousand at Mangshi; Bodyguards Yulin and Pu'erpu with five hundred also at Zanda; Bodyguards Hengshanbao and Yongshun Commander Chang Baozhu with three thousand at Yongchang; Guangdong Right Wing Commander Fan Jingwen with one thousand at Dianning; Jingzhou General Yongrui, Sichuan Deputy Lieutenant-General Yalang'a, and Military Commissioner Wufu with six thousand at Pu'er; and one thousand Tengyue troops under Miankang's additional command.

sentences.zh: 防守嚴密，邊以無事。

translations.literal: Defenses were strict; the border remained quiet.
translations.idiomatic: With defenses tight, the border remained quiet.

sentences.zh: 帝以緬人狡惡，思出偏師疑之，使其疲於奔命。

translations.literal: The emperor, deeming the Burmese cunning and vicious, considered sending a flanking force to harass them and wear them out with constant movement.
translations.idiomatic: Deeming the Burmese cunning and vicious, the emperor considered sending a flanking force to harass them and wear them out.

sentences.zh: 欲出九龍江及舊小，皆不果。

translations.literal: Plans to advance via the Jiulong River and Jiuxiao were both abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Plans to advance via the Jiulong River and Jiuxiao both came to nothing.

sentences.zh: 阿裏袞乃議剿戛鳩。

translations.literal: Arigun then proposed suppressing Gajiu.
translations.idiomatic: Arigun then proposed a punitive strike against Gajiu.

sentences.zh: 十一月，阿桂至永昌，聞信馳往會師討之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Agui reached Yongchang; hearing the news he hurried to join forces and attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Agui reached Yongchang and, hearing the plan, hurried to join the expedition.

sentences.zh: 十二月，出關，焚數寨，殲其眾數百人，止丹山。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they crossed the pass, burned several stockades, wiped out several hundred of the enemy, and halted at Danshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they crossed the frontier, burned several stockades, killed several hundred rebels, and halted at Danshan.

sentences.zh: 濮夷團五卒者，率四十餘戶來降，遷之盞達。

translations.literal: Tuan Wuzu of the Pu tribes, leading more than forty households, came to surrender and was resettled at Zanda.
translations.idiomatic: Tuan Wuzu of the Pu tribes, leading more than forty households, surrendered and was resettled at Zanda.

sentences.zh: 三十四年二月，經略傅恆發京師，帝御太和殿授以敕印。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, second month, Commander-in-Chief Fu Heng departed the capital; the emperor presided at the Hall of Supreme Harmony and conferred the edict and seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year, second month, Commander-in-Chief Fu Heng left the capital; the emperor received him at the Hall of Supreme Harmony and conferred the edict and seal.

sentences.zh: 或告傅恆曰：「元伐緬，由阿禾、阿昔二江以進。

translations.literal: Someone told Fu Heng: "When the Yuan attacked Burma, they advanced by the Ahe and Axi rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Fu Heng: "When the Yuan invaded Burma they advanced by the Ahe and Axi rivers.

sentences.zh: 今其跡不可考，意其為大金沙江無疑。

translations.literal: Their course can no longer be traced; they were surely the Great Golden Sand River.
translations.idiomatic: Those routes can no longer be traced; they were almost certainly the Great Irrawaddy.

sentences.zh: 前鄂寧言騰越之銀江，下通新街，南甸之檳榔江，流注蠻暮，兩江皆從萬山中行，石磡層布，舟楫不可施。

translations.literal: Formerly E'ning said that Tengyue's Yin River ran down to Xinjie, and Nandian's Betel-nut River flowed into Mangmu; both rivers ran through myriad mountains with layered rocky shoals, and boats could not be used.
translations.idiomatic: E'ning had reported that Tengyue's Yin River ran down to Xinjie and Nandian's Betel-nut River flowed into Mangmu; both ran through rugged mountains with layered shoals where boats could not pass.

sentences.zh: 若於近江地為舟具，使兵扛運至江滸，合成之以入於江，下阿瓦，既速且可免運糧，而師期亦較早一二月，緬人必不暇設備。

translations.literal: If boats were built near the rivers, soldiers carried the parts to the banks, assembled them, and entered the river downstream to Ava, it would be both faster and spare grain transport; the campaign schedule would also be one or two months earlier, and the Burmese would surely have no time to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: If boats were prefabricated near the rivers, carried in pieces to the banks, assembled, and launched downstream to Ava, the advance would be faster, grain transport unnecessary, and the campaign could begin one or two months sooner—before the Burmese could prepare.

sentences.zh: 又以一隊渡江而西，覆其木梳舊巢。

translations.literal: And with one column crossing the river westward, their old stronghold at Mushu could be overrun.
translations.idiomatic: A second column could cross west of the river and overrun their old stronghold at Mushu.

sentences.zh: 如此，緬不足平也。」

translations.literal: Thus Burma would not be hard to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: In this way Burma could be subdued.

sentences.zh: 傅恆然其言。

translations.literal: Fu Heng agreed with this view.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng accepted the plan.

sentences.zh: 四月丙辰，至永昌，條奏進兵事宜，皆如所議。

translations.literal: On bingchen in the fourth month he reached Yongchang and submitted a detailed memorial on the advance—all as discussed.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen in the fourth month he reached Yongchang and memorialized on the advance along the lines discussed.

sentences.zh: 遂遣護軍統領伍三泰、左副都御史傅顯及哈國興，率夷人賀丙往銅壁關外相視造舟地。

translations.literal: He then dispatched Guard Commander Wu Santai, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Fu Xian, and Ha Guoxing, leading the tribesman He Bing, to survey boat-building sites beyond Tongbi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched Guard Commander Wu Santai, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Fu Xian, and Ha Guoxing, with the tribesman He Bing, to survey boat-building sites beyond Tongbi Pass.

sentences.zh: 還報野牛壩山勢爽塏，樹木茂密，且距蠻暮河一百餘里，於入江為宜。

translations.literal: On their return they reported that Wild Ox Dam had open, level terrain and dense woods, and lay more than a hundred li from the Mangmu River—suitable for entering the river.
translations.idiomatic: They reported that Wild Ox Dam offered open ground and dense timber, and lay more than a hundred li from the Mangmu River—an ideal place to launch boats.

sentences.zh: 乃令常青等率兵三千人，督湖廣工匠四百六十餘，馳往造辦。

translations.literal: Changqing and others were ordered to lead three thousand troops and supervise more than four hundred sixty Huguang craftsmen to hurry there and build the boats.
translations.idiomatic: Changqing was ordered to take three thousand troops and more than four hundred sixty Huguang craftsmen to build the boats there at once.

sentences.zh: 又使賀丙潛行招撫。

translations.literal: He Bing was also sent secretly to win over tribes by conciliation.
translations.idiomatic: He Bing was also sent secretly to win over local tribes.

sentences.zh: 賀丙者，戛鳩頭目賀洛子也。

translations.literal: He Bing was the Gajiu chieftain Heluozi.
translations.idiomatic: He Bing was Heluozi, chieftain of Gajiu.

sentences.zh: 是役也，續遣滿洲、索倫、鄂倫春、吉林、西僰、厄魯特、察哈爾，及自普洱調赴騰越之滿洲兵，共萬餘人；

translations.literal: For this campaign, Manchu, Solon, Oroqen, Jilin, Xibo, Olot, and Chahar troops were additionally dispatched, together with Manchu soldiers transferred from Pu'er to Tengyue—more than ten thousand in all;
translations.idiomatic: For this campaign more than ten thousand Manchu, Solon, Oroqen, Jilin, Xibo, Olot, and Chahar troops were sent, together with Manchu soldiers transferred from Pu'er to Tengyue;

sentences.zh: 又福建、貴州、本省昭通鎮兵，共五萬餘人。

translations.literal: And Fujian, Guizhou, and local Zhaotong garrison troops totaled more than fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Fujian, Guizhou, and local Zhaotong garrison troops added more than fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 河南、陝西、湖廣與在省曲靖各府飼養之馬，凡六萬餘匹。

translations.literal: Horses raised in Henan, Shaanxi, Huguang, and the Qujing prefectures of the province numbered more than sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: More than sixty thousand horses were raised in Henan, Shaanxi, Huguang, and the Qujing prefectures of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 益以四川工呪術之喇嘛，京城之梅針箭、沖天砲、贊叭喇、鳥槍，河南之火箭，四川之九節銅砲，湖南之鐵鹿子，廣東之阿魏，雲南省城製造之鞍屜、帳幙、旗纛、火繩、鉛藥，及鉛鐵、灰油、麻枲諸船料物，悉運往以資軍實。

translations.literal: Added to these were Sichuan lamas skilled in ritual magic; from the capital, plum-blossom arrows, sky-reaching cannon, zambala guns, and muskets; Henan rockets; Sichuan nine-section bronze cannon; Hunan iron deer-cannon; Guangdong asafetida; saddles, tents, banners, slow match, and lead shot manufactured at the Yunnan provincial capital; and boat materials such as lead, iron, lime oil, and hemp—all were transported to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: Also sent were Sichuan lamas skilled in battle rites; from the capital plum-blossom arrows, sky-reaching cannon, zambala guns, and muskets; Henan rockets; Sichuan nine-section bronze cannon; Hunan iron deer-cannon; Guangdong asafetida; saddles, tents, banners, slow match, and lead shot from the Yunnan capital; and boat materials of lead, iron, lime oil, and hemp—all to supply the army.

sentences.zh: 乃議分路進：傅恆由江西戛鳩路，阿桂由江東猛密路，阿裏袞以肩瘡未愈，由水路，都計新舊調兵二萬九千人。

translations.literal: They then planned a multi-route advance: Fu Heng by the Gajiu route west of the river, Agui by the Mengmi route east of the river, and Arigun by water because his shoulder sore had not healed—in all twenty-nine thousand newly and previously mobilized troops.
translations.idiomatic: They planned a three-pronged advance: Fu Heng by the Gajiu route west of the river, Agui by the Mengmi route east of the river, and Arigun by water because his shoulder ailment had not healed—in all twenty-nine thousand newly and previously mobilized troops.

sentences.zh: 其由戛鳩路者，滿州兵一千五百人，護軍統領伍三泰，侍衛玉麟、納木劄、五福、鄂甯、烏爾袞保，參領滿都虎、德保領之；

translations.literal: Those on the Gajiu route: one thousand five hundred Manchu troops under Guard Commander Wu Santai, Bodyguards Yulin, Namuzha, Wufu, E'ning, and Wu'ergunbao, and company commanders Manduhu and Debao;
translations.idiomatic: The Gajiu column comprised one thousand five hundred Manchu troops under Guard Commander Wu Santai, Bodyguards Yulin, Namuzha, Wufu, E'ning, and Wu'ergunbao, and company commanders Manduhu and Debao;

sentences.zh: 吉林兵五百人，護軍統領索諾木策淩、侍衛占坡圖領之；

translations.literal: five hundred Jilin troops under Guard Commander Suonomuceling and Bodyguard Zhanpotu;
translations.idiomatic: five hundred Jilin troops under Guard Commander Suonomuceling and Bodyguard Zhanpotu;

sentences.zh: 索倫兵二千人，副都統呼爾起、奎林、莽克察，侍衛塔尼、布克車德、受菩薩，參領占皮納領之；

translations.literal: two thousand Solon troops under Deputy Lieutenant-Generals Hu'erqi, Kuilin, and Mangkecha, Bodyguards Tani, Bukechede, and Shoupusa, and company commander Zhanpina;
translations.idiomatic: two thousand Solon troops under Deputy Lieutenant-Generals Hu'erqi, Kuilin, and Mangkecha, Bodyguards Tani, Bukechede, and Shoupusa, and company commander Zhanpina;

sentences.zh: 鄂倫春兵三百人，侍衛成果領之；

translations.literal: three hundred Oroqen troops under Bodyguard Chengguo;
translations.idiomatic: three hundred Oroqen troops under Bodyguard Chengguo;

sentences.zh: 厄魯特兵三百人，侍衛鄂尼、積爾噶爾領之；

translations.literal: three hundred Olot troops under Bodyguards E'ni and Ji'erga'er;
translations.idiomatic: three hundred Olot troops under Bodyguards E'ni and Ji'erga'er;

sentences.zh: 綠營兵四千人，提督哈國興，開化鎮總兵永平及德福領之。

translations.literal: four thousand Green Standard troops under Military Commissioner Ha Guoxing, Kaihua commander Yongping, and Defu.
translations.idiomatic: and four thousand Green Standard troops under Military Commissioner Ha Guoxing, Kaihua Commander Yongping, and Defu.

sentences.zh: 其由猛密路者，滿洲兵二千人，副都統綿康、豐安、常保柱，侍衛海蘭察、瑪格、喬蘇爾、興兆、普爾普領之；

translations.literal: Those on the Mengmi route: two thousand Manchu troops under Deputy Lieutenant-Generals Miankang, Feng'an, and Chang Baozhu, and Bodyguards Hailancha, Mage, Qiaosu'er, Xingzhao, and Pu'erpu;
translations.idiomatic: The Mengmi column comprised two thousand Manchu troops under Deputy Lieutenant-Generals Miankang, Feng'an, and Chang Baozhu, and Bodyguards Hailancha, Mage, Qiaosu'er, Xingzhao, and Pu'erpu;

sentences.zh: 索倫兵一千人，散秩大臣葛布舒，侍衛額森退領之；

translations.literal: one thousand Solon troops under Minister without Portfolio Gebashu and Bodyguard Esentui;
translations.idiomatic: one thousand Solon troops under Minister without Portfolio Gebashu and Bodyguard Esentui;

sentences.zh: 厄魯特兵三百人，侍衛巴朗領之；

translations.literal: three hundred Olot troops under Bodyguard Balang;
translations.idiomatic: three hundred Olot troops under Bodyguard Balang;

sentences.zh: 綠營兵四千人，曲尋鎮總兵常青，永北鎮總兵馬彪，楚姚鎮總兵于文煥領之。

translations.literal: four thousand Green Standard troops under Qujing commander Changqing, Yongbei commander Ma Biao, and Chuyao commander Yu Wenhuan.
translations.idiomatic: and four thousand Green Standard troops under Qujing Commander Changqing, Yongbei Commander Ma Biao, and Chuyao Commander Yu Wenhuan.

sentences.zh: 其由水路者，健銳營兵五百人，侍衛烏爾圖納遜、奈庫納領之；

translations.literal: Those by water: five hundred Elite Vanguard troops under Bodyguards Wu'ertunaxun and Naikuna;
translations.idiomatic: The river column comprised five hundred Elite Vanguard troops under Bodyguards Wu'ertunaxun and Naikuna;

sentences.zh: 吉林水師五百人，副都統明亮，侍衛豐盛額領之；

translations.literal: five hundred Jilin naval troops under Deputy Lieutenant-General Mingliang and Bodyguard Fengsheng'e;
translations.idiomatic: five hundred Jilin naval troops under Deputy Lieutenant-General Mingliang and Bodyguard Fengsheng'e;

sentences.zh: 福建水師兵二千人，福建提督葉相德，福建建甯鎮總兵依昌阿領之。

translations.literal: two thousand Fujian naval troops under Fujian Military Commissioner Ye Xiangde and Jianning commander Yichang'a.
translations.idiomatic: and two thousand Fujian naval troops under Fujian Military Commissioner Ye Xiangde and Jianning Commander Yichang'a.

sentences.zh: 又令副都統鐵保，侍衛永瑞領成都滿洲兵一千二百人，侍衛富興、蒙古爾岱、鄂蘭、必拉爾海領西僰兵一千人，提督本進忠、臨元鎮總兵吳士勝領綠營兵二千二百人，分守驛站。

translations.literal: Deputy Lieutenant-General Tiebao and Bodyguard Yongrui were also ordered to lead one thousand two hundred Chengdu Manchu troops; Bodyguards Fuxing, Menggu'erdai, E'lan, and Bilahai one thousand Xibo troops; and Military Commissioner Ben Jinzhong and Linyuan commander Wu Shisheng two thousand two hundred Green Standard troops—to garrison relay stations in separate posts.
translations.idiomatic: Deputy Lieutenant-General Tiebao and Bodyguard Yongrui were assigned one thousand two hundred Chengdu Manchu troops; Bodyguards Fuxing, Menggu'erdai, E'lan, and Bilahai one thousand Xibo troops; and Military Commissioner Ben Jinzhong and Linyuan Commander Wu Shisheng two thousand two hundred Green Standard troops to garrison relay stations along the route.

sentences.zh: 又令侍衛諾爾奔領滿洲兵五百人，永順鎮總兵孫爾桂領綠營兵一千人，屯宛頂，以牽制木邦之賊。

translations.literal: Bodyguard Nuo'erben was also ordered to lead five hundred Manchu troops and Yongshun commander Sun Ergui one thousand Green Standard troops to encamp at Wanding and pin down the Mohnyin rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Bodyguard Nuo'erben with five hundred Manchu troops and Yongshun Commander Sun Ergui with one thousand Green Standard troops were posted at Wanding to pin down the Mohnyin rebels.

sentences.zh: 又令雅朗阿領荊州滿洲兵二千人，普洱鎮總兵喀木齊布領綠營兵一千五百人，駐守普洱。

translations.literal: Yalang'a was also ordered to lead two thousand Jingzhou Manchu troops and Pu'er commander Kamuqibu one thousand five hundred Green Standard troops to garrison Pu'er.
translations.idiomatic: Yalang'a with two thousand Jingzhou Manchu troops and Pu'er Commander Kamuqibu with one thousand five hundred Green Standard troops were posted at Pu'er.

sentences.zh: 分置略定，而賀丙往戛鳩招撫孟拱，挾其頭目脫烏猛以來。

translations.literal: With deployments roughly settled, He Bing went to Gajiu to win over Menggong by conciliation and brought its chieftain Tuowumeng with him.
translations.idiomatic: With deployments settled, He Bing went to Gajiu to win over Menggong and returned with its chieftain Tuowumeng.

sentences.zh: 其言曰：「上年懵駁遣頭目盞拉機以千人守猛戛，需索煩重，土司畏其偪，避往戶工。

translations.literal: He said: "Last year Mengbo sent the chieftain Zhanlaji with a thousand men to garrison Mengga; their exactions were heavy and troublesome; the native chieftain, fearing their pressure, fled to Hugong.
translations.idiomatic: Tuowumeng reported: "Last year Mengbo sent the chieftain Zhanlaji with a thousand men to hold Mengga; their exactions were oppressive, and the local chieftain, fearing them, fled to Hugong.

sentences.zh: 孟拱人苦緬人魚肉久矣，聞大軍來，皆呀呷忻喜。

translations.literal: The people of Menggong have long suffered under Burmese oppression; hearing the great army was coming, all rejoiced aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Menggong have long suffered under Burmese oppression; when they heard the imperial army was coming, they rejoiced aloud.

sentences.zh: 請由戛鳩濟江出孟拱。

translations.literal: They request to cross the river from Gajiu and emerge at Menggong.
translations.idiomatic: They ask that the army cross from Gajiu and advance on Menggong.

sentences.zh: 孟拱米穀多，可以佐軍食。

translations.literal: Menggong has abundant grain and can supplement army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Menggong has abundant grain and can supply the army.

sentences.zh: 頭目歸，當集舟於江以待。」

translations.literal: When the chieftain returns, boats will be gathered on the river to await you.
translations.idiomatic: When I return, boats will be gathered on the river to await the army.

sentences.zh: 傅恆上言：「孟拱遣大頭目來，稱歸備舟以候官兵過渡。

translations.literal: Fu Heng memorialized: "Menggong has sent a senior chieftain saying that on his return he will prepare boats to await the crossing of the imperial troops.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng reported: "Menggong has sent a senior chieftain pledging to prepare boats for the army's crossing on his return.

sentences.zh: 臣思野牛壩造舟之役，賊早有見聞，若於西岸設伏沿江拒我，未易渡也。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that the boat-building at Wild Ox Dam has long been known to the rebels; if they set ambushes on the west bank along the river to block us, crossing will not be easy.
translations.idiomatic: The boat-building at Wild Ox Dam is already known to the enemy; if they ambush the west bank it will be hard to cross.

sentences.zh: 今忽由戛鳩過江，先從陸路據蠻暮西岸，已出賊意計之外。

translations.literal: Now to cross suddenly from Gajiu and first seize the west bank of Mangmu by land is already beyond the rebels' expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Crossing suddenly from Gajiu and seizing the west bank of Mangmu by land would take the enemy by surprise.

sentences.zh: 且自戛鳩渡後，可將舟楫順流放至蠻暮，添備東岸官軍過渡。

translations.literal: Moreover, after crossing from Gajiu, boats can be floated downstream to Mangmu to help the east-bank imperial troops cross.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing at Gajiu, boats can be floated downstream to Mangmu to ferry the east-bank column as well.

sentences.zh: 如造舟處有緩急，我兵在西岸，乘舟往來策應亦最便利。

translations.literal: If the boat-building site meets urgency, our troops on the west bank can ride boats back and forth to support one another most conveniently.
translations.idiomatic: If the boat-builders meet trouble, troops on the west bank can ferry back and forth most easily to support them.

sentences.zh: 臣傅恆謹先統兵進發，阿裏袞、阿桂偕往野牛壩督辦船工。」

translations.literal: Your servant Fu Heng respectfully will first lead the army forward; Arigun and Agui will go together to Wild Ox Dam to supervise the boat work."
translations.idiomatic: I, Fu Heng, will lead the advance; Arigun and Agui will supervise boat-building at Wild Ox Dam."

sentences.zh: 癸卯，次盞達，分道行，阿里袞固請從傅恆。

translations.literal: On guimao they halted at Zanda and marched by separate routes; Arigun earnestly requested to follow Fu Heng.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the army halted at Zanda and divided; Arigun insisted on accompanying Fu Heng.

sentences.zh: 庚申，出萬仞關。

translations.literal: On gengshen they passed out through Wanren Pass.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen they crossed Wanren Pass.

sentences.zh: 八月癸丑，次允帽。

translations.literal: On guichou in the eighth month they halted at Yunmao.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou in the eighth month they halted at Yunmao.

sentences.zh: 允帽，江滸也。

translations.literal: Yunmao was on the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: Yunmao stood on the riverbank.

sentences.zh: 賀丙、脫烏猛以舟三十餘來迎。

translations.literal: He Bing and Tuowumeng came to meet them with more than thirty boats.
translations.idiomatic: He Bing and Tuowumeng came to meet them with more than thirty boats.

sentences.zh: 丙子，次孟拱。

translations.literal: On bingzi they halted at Menggong.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the army halted at Menggong.

sentences.zh: 土司渾覺竄往節東，蹤跡之，獲其小妻並頭目興堂劄，原往尋渾覺，縱之，即日偕以來，獻象四。

translations.literal: The native chieftain Hunjue fled toward Jiedong; tracking him, they captured his concubine and the chieftain Xingtangzha; originally sent to seek Hunjue, they released him; on the same day he came together with Hunjue and presented four elephants.
translations.idiomatic: The native chieftain Hunjue had fled toward Jiedong. Troops tracked him down and seized his concubine and the chieftain Xingtangzha. Xingtangzha had been sent to find Hunjue; they released him, and that same day he returned with Hunjue and presented four elephants.

sentences.zh: 傅恆令其人持大纛騎以先，夷人望見皆驚駭。

translations.literal: Fu Heng ordered his men to ride ahead carrying a great banner; when the tribesmen saw it they were all terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng had his men ride ahead bearing a great standard; the local tribesmen were struck with terror at the sight.

sentences.zh: 而予渾覺銀萬兩，市牛數千頭，米數千石，以給軍。

translations.literal: And they gave Hunjue ten thousand taels of silver, purchased several thousand head of cattle and several thousand shi of rice, to supply the army.
translations.idiomatic: They paid Hunjue ten thousand taels of silver and bought several thousand cattle and several thousand shi of rice to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 時阿桂以七月戊申次野牛壩。

translations.literal: At this time Agui on wushen in the seventh month halted at Wild Ox Dam.
translations.idiomatic: Agui halted at Wild Ox Dam on wushen in the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 舟工畢，八月乙酉，進次蠻暮。

translations.literal: When the boat work was finished, on yiyou in the eighth month they advanced and halted at Mangmu.
translations.idiomatic: Boat-building finished; on yiyou in the eighth month they advanced to Mangmu.

sentences.zh: 初，官兵之裹糧兩月也，議以進剿為始；

translations.literal: At first, when the imperial troops carried two months' rations, it was agreed that supply transport from the interior would begin with the advance to suppress the rebels;
translations.idiomatic: Initially the troops carried two months' rations, with inland supply to begin once the punitive campaign started;

sentences.zh: 而督工時仍令內地饋運，總督明德面諾之，不為具。

translations.literal: yet when supervising the work they still ordered supply from the interior; Governor-General Mingde agreed face to face but did not provide it.
translations.idiomatic: yet the boat-builders were still told inland supply would come; Governor-General Mingde agreed to his face but never arranged it.

sentences.zh: 及是，移檄往促，始令騰越州發運。

translations.literal: At this point, after dispatching a letter to urge him, he finally ordered Tengyue prefecture to send supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Only after an urgent dispatch was sent did he order Tengyue to begin transport.

sentences.zh: 泥深道遠，經月不能至。

translations.literal: The roads were deep in mud and far; a month passed and supplies could not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: The roads were muddy and long; a month passed without delivery.

sentences.zh: 乃奏糧運遲誤狀，降明德江蘇巡撫，以阿思哈代之。

translations.literal: They then memorialized on the delay in grain transport; Mingde was demoted to Jiangsu governor, and Asiha was appointed in his place.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial on the supply delay was sent; Mingde was demoted to governor of Jiangsu and replaced by Asiha.

sentences.zh: 九月壬辰，阿桂由蠻暮進至新街。

translations.literal: On renchen in the ninth month Agui advanced from Mangmu to Xinjie.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen in the ninth month Agui marched from Mangmu to Xinjie.

sentences.zh: 舟成，將出江口，賊人從猛戛來逆戰，阿桂伏兵甘立寨。

translations.literal: The boats were completed; as they were about to leave the river mouth, rebels from Mengga came to fight them head-on; Agui ambushed them and established camp at Ganli.
translations.idiomatic: With the boats ready and the fleet debouching from the river mouth, rebels from Mengga attacked; Agui ambushed them and encamped at Ganli.

sentences.zh: 賊至，水陸奮擊，發巨砲，沉其舟，譟而從之，笳鼓競作，賊大沮，退走。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, troops fought fiercely by land and water, fired great guns, sank their boats, clamored and pursued them; horns and drums sounded together; the rebels were greatly dismayed and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, the army attacked by land and water, firing great guns, sinking their boats, and pursuing with a clamor of horns and drums. The enemy broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 先是傅恆在江西，文報越兩三日輒一至，自孟拱而南，信益稀。

translations.literal: Previously, when Fu Heng was on the west bank, dispatches arrived every two or three days; south of Menggong, news grew ever rarer.
translations.idiomatic: While Fu Heng was on the west bank, reports had arrived every two or three days; south of Menggong they grew increasingly scarce.

sentences.zh: 阿桂聞蒼浦、蠻岡間有伏戎，乃募夷間道以書往訊。

translations.literal: Agui heard there were ambushing soldiers between Cangpu and Mangang; he hired tribal guides by secret route to send a letter and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of ambushes between Cangpu and Mangang, Agui hired tribal guides to carry a letter by back trails and inquire.

sentences.zh: 及伊犁將軍伊勒圖、總督阿思哈奉命皆至軍中，乃以兵二千屬伊勒圖渡江迎傅恆，並令玉麟、哈青阿率兵據西岸以待。

translations.literal: When Ili General Iletu and Governor-General Asiha arrived at the army by order, two thousand troops were assigned to Iletu to cross the river and meet Fu Heng, and Yulin and Haqing'a were ordered to lead troops and hold the west bank in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ili General Iletu and Governor-General Asiha reached headquarters, Agui gave Iletu two thousand men to cross the river and meet Fu Heng, and ordered Yulin and Haqing'a to hold the west bank.

sentences.zh: 伊勒圖渡江遇賊，擊走之，柵賊一夕皆遁去。

translations.literal: Iletu crossed the river, met rebels, routed them; the rebels in the stockades all fled overnight.
translations.idiomatic: Iletu crossed, routed the enemy, and overnight the stockade garrisons all fled.

sentences.zh: 傅恆率十八騎，以是月戊申抵哈坎。

translations.literal: Fu Heng led eighteen horsemen and on wushen of that month reached Hakan.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng with eighteen riders reached Hakan on wushen that month.

sentences.zh: 是時緬人列船江岸，且於沙洲及林莽間樹柵以守。

translations.literal: At this time the Burmese lined boats along the riverbank and also set up stockades on sandbars and in the forested wilds to defend.
translations.idiomatic: The Burmese lined the bank with boats and built stockades on sandbars and in the brush.

sentences.zh: 十月戊午，傅恆及阿桂督水師擊之，侍衛阿爾蘇納首先乘小舟沖入，眾繼進，奪其柵，獲旗纛器械無算，殲頭目賓啞得諾；

translations.literal: On wuwu in the tenth month Fu Heng and Agui directed the naval force to attack; Bodyguard Aersuna was first to charge in a small boat, the rest followed, seized their stockades, captured countless banners, standards, and weapons, and killed the chieftain Binyadenuo;
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu in the tenth month Fu Heng and Agui led the fleet in attack. Bodyguard Aersuna was first into the enemy lines in a light boat; the rest followed, took the stockades, captured countless banners and arms, and killed the chieftain Binyadenuo;

sentences.zh: 而阿裏袞、伊勒圖攻西岸諸柵，賊皆棄而走。

translations.literal: meanwhile Arigun and Iletu attacked the stockades on the west bank, and the rebels all abandoned them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Arigun and Iletu meanwhile stormed the west-bank stockades, which the enemy abandoned and fled.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，傅恆、阿桂循江東岸，伍三泰、常青循江西岸，阿裏袞、伊勒圖率水師並進。

translations.literal: On bingyin Fu Heng and Agui moved along the east bank of the river, Wu Santai and Changqing along the west bank, and Arigun and Iletu led the naval force forward together.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Fu Heng and Agui marched along the east bank, Wu Santai and Changqing along the west, while Arigun and Iletu advanced with the fleet.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，阿裏袞以瘡甚卒於舟。

translations.literal: On dingmao Arigun died of severe sores on the boat.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao Arigun died aboard ship of festering wounds.

sentences.zh: 伊勒圖領其眾已抵老官屯。

translations.literal: Iletu leading his troops had already reached Laoguanshun.
translations.idiomatic: Iletu, now commanding his force, had already reached Laoguanshun.

sentences.zh: 賊柵徑圍三里許，柵尾迤邐屬於江中，瀦水可泊船。

translations.literal: The rebel stockade was about three li in circumference; its tail wound gradually into the river, where pooled water could moor boats.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel stockade was nearly three li around; its rear curved into the river, where backwater could hold boats.

sentences.zh: 柵以巨木深入土中，外週三壕，壕外橫臥大樹，銳其枝末外向，蓋其大頭目布拉莽儻所居也。

translations.literal: The stockade had huge logs driven deep into the earth, three moats encircling outside; beyond the moats lay great trees horizontally, their branch tips sharpened and pointing outward—this was where the great chieftain Bulamangtang dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Massive logs were sunk deep into the ground, ringed by three moats; beyond the moats lay felled trees with sharpened branches pointing outward—the stronghold of the great chieftain Bulamangtang.

sentences.zh: 西岸頭目得楞孝楞率船一百三十、兵三千，起兩柵。

translations.literal: On the west bank the chieftain Delengxiaoleng led one hundred thirty boats and three thousand soldiers and built two stockades.
translations.idiomatic: On the west bank Chieftain Delengxiaoleng fielded one hundred thirty boats and three thousand men and erected two stockades.

sentences.zh: 及夕，柵木杪皆懸火。

translations.literal: By evening, fire was hung at the tips of the stockade timbers.
translations.idiomatic: By nightfall fires blazed at the tips of every stockade post.

sentences.zh: 有頃，鼓登登，雜以管籥侏離之歌，傳呼以達於江西，遠近相和，竟曉乃輟，而老官屯南巴窪、章薄賊，皆築柵以為應援。

translations.literal: Before long drums sounded dong-dong, mixed with piping and barbarian songs; shouts carried across to the west bank, near and far answering one another until dawn before ceasing; south of Laoguanshun the rebels at Bawa and Zhangbo all built stockades in support.
translations.idiomatic: Soon drums beat steadily, mingled with pipes and tribal song; cries carried to the west bank and echoed back through the night until dawn. Rebels at Bawa and Zhangbo south of Laoguanshun also threw up stockades in support.

sentences.zh: 庚午，進攻其柵，經略將軍親摩壘。

translations.literal: On gengwu they advanced to attack the stockade; the frontier-pacifying general himself inspected the ramparts at close range.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu they assaulted the stockade; the commanding general inspected the walls in person.

sentences.zh: 總兵德福中槍，逾日卒。

translations.literal: Brigadier Defu was struck by a musket ball and died the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier Defu was shot and died the following day.

sentences.zh: 乃令舟師絕兩柵中，下泊於柵南，斷賊江中援救。

translations.literal: They then ordered the naval force to pass between the two stockades and anchor south of the stockade, cutting off rebel relief across the river.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet was sent between the two stockades to anchor south of the fort and sever river-borne relief.

sentences.zh: 發威遠大砲，砲重三千斤，子三十餘斤，聲如奔雷，遇木輒洞以過，柵不為塌。

translations.literal: They fired the Weiyuan great cannon, weighing three thousand jin, with balls of more than thirty jin; its roar was like rolling thunder; wherever it met timber it pierced through, yet the stockade did not collapse.
translations.idiomatic: They brought up the Weiyuan great gun—weighing three thousand jin, firing thirty-jin balls with thunderous report. It punched through timber but could not bring the stockade down.

sentences.zh: 又改用火攻之法，先以杆牌禦槍砲，眾挾膏薪隨之，百牌齊進，逾壕抵柵；

translations.literal: They then changed to fire attack: first shield-bearers with pole-shields to ward off muskets and cannon, the rest carrying kindling following; a hundred shields advanced together, crossed the moats, and reached the stockade;
translations.idiomatic: They turned to fire: shieldmen with pole-screens first, troops with kindling behind; a hundred teams advanced together, crossed the moats, and reached the palisade;

sentences.zh: 而江自四更大霧起，迄平旦始息，柵木沾潤不能爇，兼值反風，遂卻。

translations.literal: but from the fourth watch a great fog rose on the river until dawn before clearing; the stockade timbers were damp and would not burn; moreover a contrary wind arose, and they withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: A thick fog rose from the fourth watch until dawn; the timbers were too wet to catch, and a headwind sprang up—they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 又取生革為長鐶鉤之，力急鐶輒斷；

translations.literal: They next took raw hide to make long ring-hooks and hooked the stockade; when force was applied the rings always broke;
translations.idiomatic: They tried long hide ropes with hooks; under strain the hide rings snapped;

sentences.zh: 乃伐箐中數百丈老藤，夜往鉤其柵，役數千指曳之，輒為賊斧斷。

translations.literal: then they cut several hundred zhang of old vines in the ravine, went by night to hook the stockade, and set thousands of hands to drag; each time the vines were hacked through by rebel axes.
translations.idiomatic: Then they cut hundreds of zhang of old vines in the ravines, hooked the stockade by night, and set thousands of men to haul—each time rebel axes severed the vines.

sentences.zh: 總兵馬彪乃闕隧窌藥其中，深數十丈，藥發，柵突高起丈餘，賊號駭；

translations.literal: Brigadier Mabiao then dug a tunnel beneath the stockade and placed powder in it, dozens of zhang deep; when the powder exploded the stockade suddenly rose more than a zhang; the rebels cried out in terror;
translations.idiomatic: Brigadier Mabiao mined under the stockade, packing a shaft dozens of zhang deep; the blast heaved the palisade more than a zhang into the air, and the garrison screamed in terror;

sentences.zh: 俄柵忽落平地，又起又落者三，遂不復動。

translations.literal: soon the stockade suddenly dropped to level ground, rose and fell three times, and then no longer moved.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade dropped back to earth, heaved and fell three times, then lay still.

sentences.zh: 蓋柵坡迤下，而地道平進，故土厚不能迸裂也。

translations.literal: For the stockade sloped downward, while the tunnel ran level; the earth was thick and could not burst apart.
translations.idiomatic: The stockade stood on a slope while the mine ran level; the earth was too deep to blow apart effectively.

sentences.zh: 賊自巴窪、章薄來鉛丸、火藥、糧米，卒不得斷絕，是以無逃志。

translations.literal: Rebels from Bawa and Zhangbo brought lead shot, gunpowder, and grain; these could never be cut off, and so they had no will to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Supply trains from Bawa and Zhangbo kept lead, powder, and grain flowing; with no hope of cutting them off, the garrison would not flee.

sentences.zh: 然懵駁聞新街之敗，大懼，而攻圍日久，死傷者多。

translations.literal: Yet Mengbo, hearing of the defeat at Xinjie, was greatly afraid; the siege had dragged on long and casualties were many.
translations.idiomatic: Mengbo, hearing of the defeat at Xinjie, was terrified; the long siege had inflicted heavy casualties.

sentences.zh: 十一月己丑，布拉莽儻乃遣使求罷兵。

translations.literal: On jichou in the eleventh month Bulamangtang sent an envoy requesting a ceasefire.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou in the eleventh month Bulamangtang sent envoys seeking peace.

sentences.zh: 明日，復以懵駁書至。

translations.literal: The next day a letter from Mengbo also arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The next day a letter from Mengbo arrived as well.

sentences.zh: 傅恆、阿桂召諸將問可否，諸將皆言懵駁從阿瓦致書，非震悚誠切不出此，可借此息兵。

translations.literal: Fu Heng and Agui summoned the generals to ask whether they agreed; all the generals said Mengbo's letter came from Ava; unless he were truly terrified he would not write thus—they could use this to halt the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Heng and Agui consulted the generals, who agreed: a letter from Ava meant genuine fear; they could use it to stop the war.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，作檄答之，言：「汝國欲貸天討，必繕表入貢，還所拘縶官兵，永不犯邊境。

translations.literal: On renchen they drafted a reply proclaiming: "If your country wishes to be spared Heaven's punishment, you must draw up a memorial and send tribute, return the imperial officers you hold captive, and never again violate the border.
translations.idiomatic: On renchen they issued a reply: "To be spared imperial retribution, your country must submit a memorial and tribute, release the captive imperial officers, and never again violate the frontier.

sentences.zh: 如撤兵背約，明年復當深入，不汝貸也。」

translations.literal: If you withdraw troops yet break the agreement, next year we shall advance deep again and show you no mercy."
translations.idiomatic: Break the terms after we withdraw, and next year we march deep again—without mercy."

sentences.zh: 癸巳，緬十三頭目來議事，乃遣明亮、海蘭察、哈青阿、明仁、哈國興、常青、馬彪、依常阿、于文煥、雅爾姜阿等會議，申諭所約三事，頭目皆拱手聽命。

translations.literal: On guisi thirteen Burmese chieftains came to negotiate; Mingliang, Hailancha, Haqing'a, Mingren, Haguoxing, Changqing, Mabiao, Yichang'a, Yu Wenhuan, Ya'erjiang'a, and others were sent to confer; the three agreed matters were reiterated, and the chieftains all clasped hands and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi thirteen Burmese chiefs came to parley. Mingliang, Hailancha, Haqing'a, Mingren, Haguoxing, Changqing, Mabiao, Yichang'a, Yu Wenhuan, Ya'erjiang'a, and others met them, restated the three conditions, and the chiefs assented with folded hands.

sentences.zh: 哈國興曰：「汝國僻在海裔，不知籓臣典禮，汝入貢當具表文，文首行書『緬甸王臣某奉表大皇帝陛下』，與安南、高麗各外籓等。」

translations.literal: Haguoxing said: "Your country lies remote on the ocean's edge and does not know tributary ritual; when you send tribute you must prepare a memorial; the first line must read 'Burma's king's subject So-and-so presents this memorial to His Majesty the Great Emperor'—the same as Annam, Korea, and other outer feudatories."
translations.idiomatic: Haguoxing said: "Your realm sits at the edge of the sea and knows little of tributary forms. Your memorial must open with 'Burma's king's subject [name] presents this memorial to His Majesty the Great Emperor'—as Annam, Korea, and other outer vassals do."

sentences.zh: 其管五營頭目得勒溫曰：「謹受教。」

translations.literal: The chieftain Delewen, who commanded five camps, said: "We respectfully accept instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Delewen, chief of the five camps, replied: "We accept your instruction.

sentences.zh: 目左右具書以歸。

translations.literal: The chieftains had their attendants prepare notes and departed.
translations.idiomatic: They had their attendants write it down and left.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，陳錦布、毯百餘端，獻經略將軍，而進魚鹽犒軍。

translations.literal: On dingyou they presented more than a hundred bolts of brocade and felt rugs to the frontier-pacifying general, and brought fish and salt to reward the army.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou they offered more than a hundred bolts of brocade and felt to the commanding general, with fish and salt to feast the troops.

sentences.zh: 於是焚舟鎔巨砲，奏聞，以己亥班師。

translations.literal: Thereupon they burned the boats and melted the great cannon, memorialized the court, and on jihai withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: They burned the boats, melted the great guns, reported to the throne, and withdrew on jihai.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，進虎踞關，緬人遣頭目率六十餘人送至關上。

translations.literal: On jiachen they reached Huju Pass; the Burmese sent a chieftain leading more than sixty men to escort them to the pass.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen they reached Huju Pass, where Burmese chiefs with more than sixty men escorted them to the gate.

sentences.zh: 是日奉旨以緬地瘴癘，命貰其罪，令渾覺還孟拱，而以所進四象送京師。

translations.literal: That day an edict arrived: because Burma's land is malarial, their crimes were pardoned; Hunjue was ordered back to Menggong, and the four elephants presented were sent to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That day the throne pardoned their offenses given Burma's miasmic climate, returned Hunjue to Menggong, and sent the four elephants to the capital.

sentences.zh: 伊勒圖、傅恆先後還京。

translations.literal: Iletu and Fu Heng returned to the capital one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Iletu and Fu Heng returned to the capital in turn.

sentences.zh: 木邦、蠻暮兩土司走入內地後，線甕團居緬寧之海臘，丁山、瑞團居盞達之壩築，其猛密頭人線官猛亦率眾居綿川戶南山，餘遷徙無常處。

translations.literal: After the Mohnyin and Mangmu native offices fled into the interior, Xian Wengtuan dwelt at Hailai in Mianning; Dingshan and Ruituan at Bazhu in Zhandai; the Mengmi headman Xian Guanmeng also led his people to dwell at Huchuannan Mountain in Mianchuan; the rest moved without fixed dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: After the Mohnyin and Mangmu chieftains fled inland, Xian Wengtuan settled at Hailai in Mianning, Dingshan and Ruituan at Bazhu in Zhandai, and Mengmi headman Xian Guanmeng led his followers to Huchuannan Mountain in Mianchuan; others wandered without fixed homes.

sentences.zh: 及是，移線甕團於蒙化，移瑞團、線官猛於大理，各取官莊租贍之；

translations.literal: At this time Xian Wengtuan was moved to Menghua, Ruituan and Xian Guanmeng to Dali; each was supported with rent from official estates.
translations.idiomatic: They were now resettled—Xian Wengtuan in Menghua, Ruituan and Xian Guanmeng in Dali—supported on rents from official estates.

sentences.zh: 而賀丙則從其請，居於萬仞關外之南底壩。

translations.literal: He Bing, as he had requested, was settled at Nandi Dam outside Wanren Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He Bing, at his own request, was placed at Nandi Dam beyond Wanren Pass.

sentences.zh: 其後又以召丙、叭先捧等分置於寧洱縣之蕨箕壩，而大山之侄阿隴、允帽頭目之女老安皆屬縣官，予以廩給。

translations.literal: Later Zhaobing, Baxianpeng, and others were separately settled at Jueji Dam in Ning'er county; Dashan's nephew Along and Yunmao chieftain's daughter Lao'an were both placed under county officials and given grain stipends.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zhaobing, Baxianpeng, and others were resettled at Jueji Dam in Ning'er County; Dashan's nephew Along and Yunmao chieftain's daughter Lao'an were placed under county administration with grain stipends.

sentences.zh: 猛勇頭目召工、整欠頭目召教、景海頭目召別，咸原輸誠進獻。

translations.literal: The Mengyong chieftain Zhaogong, Zhengqian chieftain Zhaojiao, and Jinghai chieftain Zhaobie all originally submitted loyalty and offered tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyong Chieftain Zhaogong, Zhengqian Chieftain Zhaojiao, and Jinghai Chieftain Zhaobie had all pledged allegiance and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 三十五年二月，因緬人貢使不至，帝令毋許奸商挾貨貿遷以利緬，且漏內地消息。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirty-fifth year, because the Burmese tribute envoys had not arrived, the Emperor ordered that unscrupulous merchants must not carry goods to trade for Burmese profit and leak news from the interior.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of year thirty-five, with no Burmese tribute mission forthcoming, the Emperor forbade merchants from profiteering with Burma and leaking inland intelligence.

sentences.zh: 時阿桂還至省城，命核所用軍裝馬匹，又命總督彰寶檄斥緬入貢使遲滯狀，使都司蘇爾相持至老官屯，布拉莽儻留之。

translations.literal: At this time Agui had returned to the provincial capital and was ordered to audit army equipment and horses used; Governor Zhang Bao was also ordered to dispatch a rebuke concerning the delay of the Burmese tribute envoys, sending Brigade Commander Su Erxiang to Laoguanshun, where Bulamangtang detained him.
translations.idiomatic: Agui returned to the provincial capital to audit equipment and horses; Governor Zhang Bao was told to rebuke Burma for delaying tribute and sent Brigade Commander Su Erxiang to Laoguanshun, where Bulamangtang held him.

sentences.zh: 阿桂回至永昌察賊狀，三十六年三月，阿桂奏言：「蠻暮、木邦、猛密三土司外，始有緬人村落，距邊已二千餘里，偏師不可深入。

translations.literal: Agui returned to Yongchang to investigate rebel conditions; in the third month of the thirty-sixth year Agui memorialized: "Beyond the three native offices of Mangmu, Mohnyin, and Mengmi, Burmese villages begin; they are already more than two thousand li from the border—a detached force cannot penetrate deep.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Yongchang to assess the enemy, Agui memorialized in the third month of year thirty-six: "Beyond Mangmu, Mohnyin, and Mengmi, Burmese villages begin more than two thousand li from the border; a partial force cannot advance far.

sentences.zh: 若出近邊，則所殲乃濮夷野人，與緬無損。

translations.literal: If operations stay near the border, what is destroyed are Pu barbarian wild men, which does Burma no harm.
translations.idiomatic: Strikes near the frontier would kill only Pu tribesmen, doing Burma no real harm.

sentences.zh: 不如休息數年，外約暹羅同時大舉。」

translations.literal: Better to rest several years and externally arrange with Siam for a coordinated major campaign."
translations.idiomatic: Better to rest a few years and coordinate a joint major campaign with Siam."

sentences.zh: 帝以大舉非計，乃罷阿桂，以溫福代之。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered a major campaign unwise, removed Agui, and replaced him with Wenfu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rejected a grand offensive, dismissed Agui, and appointed Wenfu in his place.

sentences.zh: 明年，金川反，溫福、阿桂皆赴四川。

translations.literal: The next year the Jinchuan rebellion broke out; Wenfu and Agui both went to Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the Jinchuan rebellion erupted; Wenfu and Agui were both sent to Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 而緬亦方用兵暹羅，於是暹羅滅於緬。

translations.literal: Burma was also campaigning against Siam at the time, and so Siam was destroyed by Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Burma was also at war with Siam—and Siam fell to Burma.

sentences.zh: 四十一年，金川平。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year Jinchuan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-one Jinchuan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 時緬甸先遣孟遮等五人以書呈雲南總督圖思德，總督縶之歸京師。

translations.literal: Burma had earlier sent Mengzhe and four others with a letter to Yunnan Governor Tuside; the governor seized them and sent them to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Burma had earlier sent Mengzhe and four others with a letter to Yunnan Governor Tuside, who detained them and sent them to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及是，命赴市曹觀狀，且告之故，乃縱使歸緬，而令阿桂以大學士赴永昌備邊。

translations.literal: At this point they were ordered to the execution ground to witness an execution and told the reason; then the envoys were released to return to Burma, and Agui was ordered as Grand Secretary to go to Yongchang to prepare the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: They were taken to the execution ground to witness a sentence and told why; then released to Burma, while Agui was sent to Yongchang as Grand Secretary to ready the border.

sentences.zh: 緬懼，請入貢，原出楊重英、蘇爾相，求開關互市。

translations.literal: Burma was afraid, requested to send tribute, agreed to release Yang Chongying and Su Erxiang, and asked to open the passes for mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Burma offered tribute, promised to release Yang Chongying and Su Erxiang, and asked to reopen border trade.

sentences.zh: 明年，出蘇爾相，而楊重英不至。

translations.literal: The next year Su Erxiang was released, but Yang Chongying did not come.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they released Su Erxiang—but not Yang Chongying.

sentences.zh: 四十三年，暹羅遺民起兵逐緬人復國。

translations.literal: In the forty-third year Siam's surviving people rose in arms, drove out the Burmese, and restored their kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-three Siamese survivors rose up, expelled the Burmese, and restored their kingdom.

sentences.zh: 五十一年，詔封鄭華為暹羅國王，於是緬益懼。

translations.literal: In the fifty-first year an edict enfeoffed Zheng Hua as King of Siam; Burma grew ever more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifty-one Zheng Hua was enfeoffed King of Siam—and Burma grew more afraid.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，耿馬土司罕朝瑗報言：「滾弄隔岸即緬甸木邦，緬酋孟雲遣大頭目葉渺瑞洞、細哈覺控、委盧撤亞三名，率小頭人從役百餘人，齎金葉表文，金塔及馴象八、寶石、金箔、檀香、大呢、象牙、漆盒諸物，絨氈、洋布四種，懇求進貢。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year Gengma native chieftain Han Chaoyuan reported: "Gunyong lies just across the river from Burma's Mohnyin; the Burmese chief Mengyun sent three great chieftains—Yemiaoruidong, Xihajuekong, and Weilucerya—leading more than a hundred minor chiefs and attendants, bearing a gold-leaf memorial, a golden pagoda, eight tame elephants, gems, gold leaf, sandalwood, broad cloth, ivory, lacquer boxes, and other goods, four kinds of felt rugs and foreign cloth, earnestly requesting to send tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifty-two Gengma chieftain Han Chaoyuan reported: "Gunyong faces Burma's Mohnyin across the river. Burmese ruler Mengyun has sent three senior chiefs—Yemiaoruidong, Xihajuekong, and Weilucerya—with more than a hundred subordinates, bearing a gold-leaf memorial, a golden pagoda, eight tame elephants, gems, gold leaf, sandalwood, woolens, ivory, lacquer boxes, felts, and foreign cloths, begging leave to present tribute.

sentences.zh: 譯其文，稱孟雲乃甕藉牙第四子，幼為僧，懵駁其長兄也。

translations.literal: Translating the text, it said Mengyun was the fourth son of Wengjiaya, had been a monk in youth, and was younger brother to Mengbo.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial named Mengyun as the fourth son of Wengjiaya—a former monk and Mengbo's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 懵駁死，子贅角牙立。

translations.literal: When Mengbo died, his son Zhuajiaoya succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Mengbo died, his son Zhuajiaoya took the throne.

sentences.zh: 孟雲次兄孟魯，以甕藉牙有兄終弟及之諭，懵駁死而子襲，非約，乃戕殺贅角牙，欲自立，國人不服，亦殺孟魯，迎孟雲立之。

translations.literal: Mengyun's second elder brother Menglu, citing Wengjiaya's instruction that brothers succeed when the elder dies, held that after Mengbo's death his son's succession violated the agreement; he murdered Zhuajiaoya and sought to rule himself; the people would not accept it and also killed Menglu, welcoming Mengyun to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyun's elder brother Menglu invoked Wengjiaya's rule of succession from brother to brother: Mengbo's son Zhuajiaoya had seized the throne unlawfully. Menglu killed Zhuajiaoya and tried to reign; the court rejected him and killed Menglu, raising Mengyun instead.

sentences.zh: 孟雲深知父子行事錯謬，感大皇帝恩德，屢欲投誠進貢，因與暹羅構釁，且移建城池，未暇備辦。

translations.literal: Mengyun deeply knew his father and brother's conduct had been wrong; moved by the Great Emperor's grace, he had long wished to submit and send tribute, but because of conflict with Siam and the relocation and building of his capital, he had had no leisure to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Mengyun acknowledged his family's errors, was grateful for the Emperor's grace, and had long wished to submit—but wars with Siam and rebuilding his capital had delayed him.

sentences.zh: 今緬甸安寧，特差頭目遵照古禮進表納貢。」

translations.literal: Now Burma is at peace; he specially dispatches chieftains to present a memorial and tribute according to ancient ritual."
translations.idiomatic: Now that Burma is at peace, he sends these chiefs to present tribute by ancient forms."

sentences.zh: 總督富綱等以聞，帝允所請，賚其使而歸之，且賚孟雲佛像、文綺、珍玩器皿。

translations.literal: Governors Fugang and others reported this; the Emperor granted the request, rewarded the envoys and sent them home, and also bestowed on Mengyun a Buddha image, brocades, and precious curios.
translations.idiomatic: Governors Fugang and others reported this; the Emperor granted the request, rewarded the envoys and sent them home, and also sent Mengyun a Buddha image, brocades, and fine gifts.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，孟雲遣使賀八旬萬壽，乞賜封，又請開關禁以通商旅，帝皆從之，封為緬甸國王，賜敕書、印信，及御製詩章、珍珠手串，遣道員、參將齎往其新都蠻得列，定十年一貢。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year Mengyun sent envoys to congratulate the Emperor's eightieth birthday, begged for enfeoffment, and again asked to open the passes and lift prohibitions for merchants; the Emperor granted all; he was enfeoffed King of Burma, given an edict, seal, imperial poems, and a pearl rosary; an intendant and regimental colonel were dispatched to his new capital Manudelie; tribute every ten years was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In year fifty-four Mengyun sent birthday congratulations for the Emperor's eightieth year, sought investiture, and asked to reopen trade. The Emperor agreed, enfeoffed him King of Burma, and sent an edict, seal, imperial poems, and a pearl rosary; an intendant and regimental colonel carried them to his new capital Manudelie. Tribute every ten years was fixed.

sentences.zh: 自是西南無緬患。

translations.literal: From this time there was no Burmese trouble in the southwest.
translations.idiomatic: After that the southwest knew no further trouble from Burma.

sentences.zh: 六十年，緬王遣使祝釐，進緬石長壽佛、貝葉緬字經、福字鐙、金海螺、銀海螺、金鑲緬刀、金柄麈尾、黃緞傘、貼金象轎、洋槍、馬鞍、象牙、犀角、孔雀、木化石、玄猴皮、各色呢、各色花布，都十有八種。

translations.literal: In the sixtieth year the Burmese king sent envoys to offer felicitations, presenting a Burma-stone longevity Buddha, a palm-leaf sutra in Burmese script, a felicity-character lamp, gold and silver conch shells, a gold-inlaid Burmese knife, a gold-handled flywhisk, a yellow satin umbrella, a gilt elephant palanquin, foreign muskets, a saddle, ivory, rhinoceros horn, a peacock, petrified wood, black monkey skin, felts of various colors, and flowered cloths of various colors—eighteen kinds in all.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixty the Burmese king sent felicitations with eighteen kinds of gifts: a Burmese-jade longevity Buddha, a palm-leaf sutra in Burmese script, a "Fortune" lamp, gold and silver conches, a gold-inlaid knife, a gold-handled flywhisk, a yellow satin umbrella, a gilt elephant litter, foreign muskets, a saddle, ivory, rhinoceros horn, a peacock, petrified wood, black monkey pelts, and assorted felts and calicos.

sentences.zh: 時有三緬盜逸入印度，緬人以五千人追之，突入印度之勢他加境，英人領土也。

translations.literal: At this time three Burmese robbers escaped into India; Burmese with five thousand men pursued them and suddenly entered Shittagaung in India—British territory.
translations.idiomatic: Three Burmese bandits fled into India; five thousand Burmese pursuers burst into Shittagaung—British territory.

sentences.zh: 英守將爾斯根詰緬人，以盜付之。

translations.literal: The British garrison commander Ersgen questioned the Burmese and handed over the robbers to them.
translations.idiomatic: British commandant Ersgen challenged the Burmese and surrendered the fugitives.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶元年，緬王復遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiaqing the Burmese king again sent envoys to court with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing year one the Burmese king again sent a tribute mission.

sentences.zh: 總督勒保以緬使甫經回國，不宜數來，檄雲南司道拒勿納。

translations.literal: Governor Lepao, because the Burmese envoys had just returned home and should not come so frequently, ordered Yunnan's circuit intendants to refuse them and not admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Lepao, arguing the envoys had just left and should not return so soon, ordered Yunnan officials to turn them away.

sentences.zh: 事聞，帝諭曰：「緬甸國王以本年國慶，特遣使臣齎表備物申虔稱賀，勒保不據實奏聞，遽行拒絕，致令使臣徒勞跋涉，殊失柔遠綏懷之意。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the Emperor instructed: "The King of Burma, on his country's anniversary this year, specially sent envoys bearing a memorial and gifts to offer sincere congratulations; Lepao did not truthfully memorial the throne but hastily refused them, causing the envoys to travel in vain—greatly violating the intent to cherish the distant and soothe them.
translations.idiomatic: Reported to the throne, the Emperor rebuked Lepao: "Burma's king sent envoys this national anniversary with tribute and sincere congratulations. Lepao neither reported truthfully nor received them, wasting their journey—contrary to policy toward distant realms.

sentences.zh: 勒保交部嚴議。」

translations.literal: Lepao was referred to the Board for strict deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Lepao was referred to the ministry for disciplinary review."

sentences.zh: 命軍機大臣擬旨曉諭緬王，頒賜蟒錦四端。

translations.literal: The Grand Council was ordered to draft an edict informing the Burmese king and bestow four bolts of python-pattern brocade.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Council was ordered to reassure the Burmese king and send four bolts of python brocade.

sentences.zh: 五年，緬甸入貢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Burma sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year five Burma sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 十年冬，緬甸復遣使叩關求入貢，以是年暹羅伐緬，有敕諭暹羅罷兵故也。

translations.literal: In the winter of the tenth year Burma again sent envoys knocking at the pass seeking to offer tribute—because that year Siam had attacked Burma and there had been an edict ordering Siam to cease fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of year ten Burma again knocked at the pass seeking tribute—Siam had attacked that year, and an edict had ordered Siam to stand down.

sentences.zh: 帝以非貢期，卻之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because it was not the tribute period, refused them.
translations.idiomatic: It was not a tribute year; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 時緬甸雖失暹羅，國勢猶盛。

translations.literal: At this time although Burma had lost Siam, its national strength was still great.
translations.idiomatic: Though Burma had lost Siam, its power remained formidable.

sentences.zh: 其疆域南盡南海，北迄孟拱，西包阿拉幹，東聯麻爾古。

translations.literal: Its territory extended south to the South Sea, north to Menggong, west embracing Arakan, east joining with Malaku.
translations.idiomatic: Its lands ran south to the South Sea, north to Menggong, west through Arakan, east to Malaku.

sentences.zh: 又有拈人之地環其東境，舊稱九十九國，多為領屬，地廣兵強。

translations.literal: There was also the land of the Nian people encircling its eastern border, formerly called the ninety-nine states, mostly its dependencies—broad territory and strong armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian peoples ringed its eastern frontier—the old "Ninety-Nine States," mostly its dependencies—vast lands and strong armies.

sentences.zh: 既東失暹羅，乃西覬印度之富，時思襲取。

translations.literal: Having already lost Siam in the east, they then looked west with covetous eyes at India's wealth, constantly thinking of raiding and seizing it.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost Siam to the east, Burma now eyed India's wealth to the west and plotted raids.

sentences.zh: 緬西北有曼尼坡部，又西有阿薩密部，緬嘗以兵攻二部，漸有從西黑特旁侵入英領之勢。

translations.literal: Northwest of Burma was the Manipur department; further west was the Assam department; Burma had several times attacked the two departments with troops, gradually developing a tendency to infiltrate British territory by way of Syhiem.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest lay Manipur and beyond it Assam; Burma had repeatedly attacked both, and was edging toward British territory via Syhiem.

sentences.zh: 西黑特居阿薩密南，為印度孟加東北境，過此即克車部，英人所保護也。

translations.literal: Syhiem lay south of Assam, on the northeastern border of Bengal in India; beyond it was the Koch department, which the British protected.
translations.idiomatic: Syhiem stood south of Assam on Bengal's northeastern frontier; beyond it lay Koch, under British protection.

sentences.zh: 緬人恃其習戰，蔑視英人，後果侵英邊，殺英戍兵，擄其人民。

translations.literal: The Burmese, relying on their skill in warfare, despised the British; afterward they indeed invaded the British border, killed British garrison soldiers, and carried off their people.
translations.idiomatic: Confident in their martial skills, the Burmese despised the British—and duly raided the frontier, killing garrison troops and taking captives.

sentences.zh: 又南侵入勢他加，英人以少兵守內府河口之刷浦黎島。

translations.literal: They also invaded Shittagaung to the south; the British with a small force garrisoned Shapuree Island at the mouth of the Naf River.
translations.idiomatic: They also struck south into Shittagaung; the British held Shapuree Island at the Naf estuary with a small garrison.

sentences.zh: 道光三年，緬人攻守島英兵，英以眾寡不敵而潰，亡數人。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daoguang, Burmese attacked the island garrison of British troops; the British, outnumbered, broke and fled, losing several men.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang year three the Burmese assaulted the island garrison; outnumbered, the British broke and lost several men.

sentences.zh: 英人來責言，緬置不答，益輕英。

translations.literal: The British came to lodge protests; Burma ignored them and paid no reply, further despising the British.
translations.idiomatic: Britain protested; Burma ignored the complaints and despised them all the more.

sentences.zh: 明年，英人伐緬，水師副提督喀姆稗兒率師進厄勒瓦諦江，即大金沙江也。

translations.literal: The next year the British attacked Burma; Rear Admiral Campbell led his fleet up the Irrawaddy River—that is, the great Irrawaddy.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Britain invaded; Rear Admiral Campbell sailed up the Irrawaddy—the great Irrawaddy River.

sentences.zh: 次仰光，緬人禦諸海口而敗，英軍遂登陸攻仰光、克曼庭村寨。

translations.literal: Next at Rangoon, the Burmese defended at the river mouths and were defeated; the British army then landed and attacked Rangoon and the villages of Kemmendine.
translations.idiomatic: At Rangoon the Burmese lost a naval battle; the British landed and took Rangoon and Kemmendine.

sentences.zh: 緬兵懼，每戰輒奔潰，然去必毀其積貯，堅壁清野以待，英人野無所掠，糧運又不繼，遂大困。

translations.literal: The Burmese troops were afraid; in every battle they fled and broke, yet when they withdrew they always destroyed their stores, fortified walls and cleared the countryside to wait; the British in the field had nothing to plunder, and grain transport could not continue, so they fell into great distress.
translations.idiomatic: Burmese troops fled every battle but scorched earth as they went—burning stores and emptying the countryside. The British found nothing to forage and supply lines failed; they were soon in dire straits.

sentences.zh: 緬王乘其敝，自阿瓦遣大隊圍攻之，英軍固守不動，緬人不能勝。

translations.literal: The Burmese king, taking advantage of their exhaustion, sent a large force from Ava to besiege them; the British army held firm without moving, and the Burmese could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The king seized the moment, sending a large force from Ava to besiege them; the British held fast and Burma could not break them.

sentences.zh: 英軍尋以巨砲反攻緬，緬軍潰。

translations.literal: Before long the British army counterattacked Burma with great cannon; the Burmese army was routed.
translations.idiomatic: The British soon counterattacked with heavy guns and routed the Burmese.

sentences.zh: 逾數月，喀姆稗兒乘間攻克艾報、墨爾階兩城，與瀕海地那悉林之地，然英軍傷病相屬，其強壯能勝戰者僅三千人，乃移病卒休養於艾報諸城，勢復振。

translations.literal: After several months Campbell seized the opportunity to capture the two cities of Pegu and Martaban and the coastal Tenasserim region; yet wounded and sick followed one after another in the British army, and those strong enough to fight were only three thousand men; they then moved the sick soldiers to recuperate in the Pegu cities, and their strength revived again.
translations.idiomatic: Months later Campbell took Pegu, Martaban, and coastal Tenasserim—but casualties mounted until only three thousand fit fighters remained. Sick troops were sent to recuperate in Pegu, and the army rallied.

sentences.zh: 進攻擺古河口之悉林工廠，與葡萄牙所築舊堡，悉取之。

translations.literal: They advanced to attack the Syriam factory at the mouth of the Bassein River and the old fort built by the Portuguese, taking them all.
translations.idiomatic: They took the Syriam factory at the Bassein estuary and the old Portuguese fort.

sentences.zh: 又克馬爾達般省。

translations.literal: They also captured Ma'erdaban province.
translations.idiomatic: They also conquered Ma'erdaban province.

sentences.zh: 緬人懼，徵鎮守阿拉幹長勝軍回援，其帥班都拉，健將也。

translations.literal: The Burmese were afraid; they recalled the Changsheng Army guarding Arakan to reinforce them; its commander Bandula was a stalwart general.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, the Burmese recalled the Changsheng Army from Arakan under the doughty general Bandula.

sentences.zh: 班都拉既至，急突英軍，不得入，乃退而集師。

translations.literal: After Bandula arrived, he urgently charged the British army but could not break in; he then withdrew and gathered his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Bandula arrived and launched a fierce assault but could not break through; he withdrew to regroup.

sentences.zh: 十一月，班都拉以眾六萬攻仰光及克曼廷村寨，不克。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Bandula with sixty thousand men attacked Rangoon and the Kemmendine villages but could not capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Bandula led sixty thousand men against Rangoon and Kemmendine without success.

sentences.zh: 還至丹阿卜，掘地營而守，喀姆稗兒於是進攻普羅美，其地西距厄勒瓦諦江約三里許。

translations.literal: Returning to Danubyu, he dug earthworks and encamped to hold them; Campbell then advanced to attack Prome, which lay about three li west of the Irrawaddy River.
translations.idiomatic: He fell back to Danubyu and dug in; Campbell then advanced on Prome, some three li west of the Irrawaddy.

sentences.zh: 明年，英軍分水陸進，將軍可敦將水師，喀姆稗兒將陸軍，會於丹阿卜，合力奪地營，緬將班都拉中砲死，遂長驅入普羅美城。

translations.literal: The next year the British army advanced by land and water; General Cotton commanded the fleet and Campbell the land army; they met at Danubyu, jointly seized the earthworks, the Burmese general Bandula was killed by cannon fire, and they then drove straight into Prome city.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Cotton's fleet and Campbell's land force converged on Danubyu, stormed the earthworks, and killed Bandula by cannon fire before marching into Prome.

sentences.zh: 時值大雨，約各休兵一月，以九月十七日為期。

translations.literal: Heavy rain fell at the time; the two sides agreed to suspend fighting for one month, with the seventeenth day of the ninth month as the deadline.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains brought a month's truce, set to end on the seventeenth of the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 入夏以來，英別將馬立生攻克阿拉幹部，並逐阿薩密北部緬人，進駐克車。

translations.literal: Since summer began, the British lieutenant Morrison had captured the Arakan department and also driven the Burmese from northern Assam, advancing to garrison Koch.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Lieutenant Morrison took Arakan, drove the Burmese from northern Assam, and garrisoned Koch.

sentences.zh: 十月，緬軍三路攻普羅美，英守將僅有歐人三千，印人二千，緬軍不能入。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Burmese army attacked Prome on three routes; the British garrison commander had only three thousand Europeans and two thousand Indians; the Burmese army could not break in.
