translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Burma assaulted Prome on three fronts with a garrison of only three thousand Europeans and two thousand Indians—the attack failed.

sentences.zh: 十二月，英人分擊緬軍，緬軍沿厄勒瓦諦江敗退，各以一萬二千人分入米投、麥龍，築壘堅守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the British divided their forces to strike the Burmese army; the Burmese army retreated in defeat along the Irrawaddy River, each division of twelve thousand men entering Meto and Mailung and building fortifications to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the British divided to attack; the Burmese fell back along the Irrawaddy, twelve thousand men each fortifying Meto and Mailung.

sentences.zh: 未幾，米投破，餘兵奔麥龍，緬人力竭，求成於英，英將允之，遣人議和款，要以四事：一，割阿拉幹、艾報、墨爾階與意愛各城歸英轄；

translations.literal: Before long Meto fell; the remaining troops fled to Mailung; the Burmese were exhausted and sought peace from the British; the British general agreed and sent men to negotiate terms, requiring four things: first, cede Arakan, Pegu, Martaban, and the various cities of Yee-ngai to British jurisdiction;
translations.idiomatic: Meto soon fell and survivors retreated to Mailung; exhausted, Burma sued for peace. The British general agreed to negotiate on four terms: first, cede Arakan, Pegu, Martaban, and Yee-ngai to British rule;

sentences.zh: 二，阿薩密部與各小部，緬人毋得干預其治權；

translations.literal: Second, the Assam department and the various small departments—Burmese were not to interfere in their governance;
translations.idiomatic: Second, Burma was not to interfere in Assam or the smaller states;

sentences.zh: 三，賠軍費一千萬羅比；

translations.literal: Third, pay ten million rupees in war costs;
translations.idiomatic: Third, pay ten million rupees in indemnity;

sentences.zh: 四，應准各國代理人駐紮緬京，且得以兵五十名為衛，英艦之入緬港者，毋得勒令繳槍彈船舵。

translations.literal: Fourth, agents of each nation were to be permitted to be stationed in the Burmese capital with a guard of fifty soldiers, and British ships entering Burmese ports were not to be compelled to surrender guns, ammunition, or rudders.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, foreign agents might station fifty guards in the capital, and British ships in Burmese ports were not to be disarmed or stripped of rudders.

sentences.zh: 議員簽押呈緬王署押，緬王不允，飭整戰備。

translations.literal: The negotiators signed and submitted it for the Burmese king's seal; the Burmese king would not agree and ordered war preparations strengthened.
translations.idiomatic: Negotiators signed and submitted the treaty for the king's seal; he refused and ordered preparations for renewed war.

sentences.zh: 英將偵知緬王無和意，明年一月十九日，攻克麥龍城，緬人復遣使議和，且徵蒲甘兵衛京城。

translations.literal: The British general learned the Burmese king had no intention of peace; on the nineteenth day of the first month of the next year he captured Mailung city; the Burmese again sent envoys to negotiate peace and also summoned Pagan troops to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the king would not yield, the British general took Mailung on the nineteenth of the first month; Burma again sent peace envoys and summoned Pagan troops to defend the capital.

sentences.zh: 英將知非王本意，進攻不已，緬廷乃使美士迫拉意斯持前署押約章，並羅比二百五十萬至英軍乞止兵，英乃撤兵去。

translations.literal: The British general knew this was not the king's true intent and continued the offensive without cease; the Burmese court then sent Maung Bare with the previously sealed treaty and two and a half million rupees to the British army begging them to cease fighting, and the British then withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: The British general knew this was not the king's will and pressed on; the court sent Maung Bare with the signed treaty and two and a half million rupees to buy a halt—and Britain withdrew.

sentences.zh: 時道光六年也。

translations.literal: It was the sixth year of Daoguang.
translations.idiomatic: This was Daoguang year six.

sentences.zh: 約成，緬國遂失西偏沿海地數部。

translations.literal: When the treaty was concluded, Burma thus lost several departments of its western coastal territory.
translations.idiomatic: The treaty cost Burma several western coastal provinces.

sentences.zh: 然緬國上下均不服此約。

translations.literal: Yet upper and lower Burma alike would not accept this treaty.
translations.idiomatic: Yet all Burma, court and country alike, rejected the treaty.

sentences.zh: 迨緬王弗極道為其弟撒拉瓦第所篡，撒拉瓦第素主排英，尤蔑視前約。

translations.literal: When King Bagyidaw was later usurped by his younger brother Tharawadi, Tharawadi had always advocated anti-British policy and especially despised the earlier treaty.
translations.idiomatic: When Tharawadi deposed his brother Bagyidaw, the new king—long an anti-British partisan—especially scorned the earlier treaty.

sentences.zh: 先是英使臣軍佐白奈駐阿瓦，與緬王齟齬而去，兩國交遂破，英政府撤回駐緬職事人。

translations.literal: Earlier the British envoy Major Baynes had been stationed at Ava; he quarreled with the Burmese king and departed; relations between the two countries were thus broken, and the British government withdrew its resident officers in Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Major Baynes, Britain's envoy at Ava, had quarreled with the king and left; diplomatic ties broke and Britain recalled its residents.

sentences.zh: 是後緬人遇英人頗暴厲，英艦至緬者，緬人常與其水手閧，英廷遣使詰責緬廷，且護以水師。

translations.literal: After this the Burmese were quite harsh toward the British; when British ships reached Burma the Burmese often brawled with their sailors; the British court sent envoys to rebuke the Burmese court and also protected them with the fleet.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Burmese treatment of Britons turned violent; sailors brawled with Burmese whenever ships called, and London protested under naval escort.

sentences.zh: 比英使至仰光，謁其督臣，語不合，英使遂以兵艦封其港，責償前英船所受損失費，要緬廷禮接英使，仰光督臣在英使前謝罪。

translations.literal: When the British envoy reached Rangoon and had audience with its governor, their words did not agree; the British envoy then blockaded the port with warships, demanded compensation for prior losses to British ships, required the Burmese court to receive the British envoy with proper ceremony, and required the Rangoon governor to apologize before the British envoy.
translations.idiomatic: When a British envoy reached Rangoon and quarreled with the governor, warships blockaded the port; Britain demanded compensation, ceremonial reception, and a public apology from the governor.

sentences.zh: 時緬王蒲甘曼嗣立，執不允。

translations.literal: At the time King Pagan Min had newly succeeded; he stubbornly refused.
translations.idiomatic: The new king Pagan Min refused.

sentences.zh: 於是英、緬再失和，而修職貢於中國如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Britain and Burma again broke relations, yet tribute missions to China continued as before.
translations.idiomatic: Britain and Burma were at odds again—but tribute to China continued unchanged.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年十一月，羅繞典奏緬國貢使入京，請變通辦理。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the third year of Xianfeng, Luo Raodian memorialized that Burmese tribute envoys were entering the capital and requested flexible handling.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Xianfeng year three, Luo Raodian reported that Burmese tribute envoys were en route and asked for special arrangements.

sentences.zh: 帝諭軍機大臣曰：「朕念緬甸國王久列籓封，貢使遠道輸誠，具徵忱悃。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed the Grand Council: "I reflect that the King of Burma has long held a feudal seal; his envoys have come from afar to convey sincerity, fully showing loyal devotion.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told the Grand Council: "Burma's king has long held investiture; envoys traveling from afar show sincere loyalty.

sentences.zh: 惟其國貢使向取道貴州、湖南、湖北進京。

translations.literal: Yet their country's envoys have always taken the route through Guizhou, Hunan, and Hubei to reach the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Their envoys have always come via Guizhou, Hunan, and Hubei.

sentences.zh: 現在粵匪未平，若令繞道而行，殊非所以示體恤。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels are not yet pacified; if they were made to detour, that would truly not be the way to show considerate care.
translations.idiomatic: The Cantonese rebels are not yet suppressed; forcing a detour would hardly show considerate care.

sentences.zh: 即傳旨其使臣，此次無庸來京，仍優予犒賞，委員護送回國。」

translations.literal: Transmit the decree at once to their envoys: this time they need not come to the capital; still grant them generous rewards, and assign officials to escort them home."
translations.idiomatic: Tell their envoys at once: this time they need not come to court; grant generous rewards and escort them home."

sentences.zh: 是年，緬、英再開戰，南方嚴城要地盡入於英，前所交還擺古部亦為英擾。

translations.literal: That year Burma and Britain again opened war; the important fortified places of the south all fell to the British, and the Bassein department previously returned was also harassed by the British.
translations.idiomatic: That year war resumed; Britain seized the south's strongholds and even raided Bassein, which had been returned.

sentences.zh: 英將道好西宣言以擺古隸英版圖。

translations.literal: The British general Dalhousie proclaimed that Bassein was annexed to British territory.
translations.idiomatic: General Dalhousie declared Bassein annexed to the British dominions.

sentences.zh: 適緬親王曼同下王於獄，自立為王，遣使說印督道好西索還擺古，英廷命軍佐雅實勿裏為擺古行政長官，且充使以報。

translations.literal: Just then the Burmese prince Mindon imprisoned the king and established himself as king; he sent envoys to urge the Governor-General Dalhousie to return Bassein; the British court appointed Colonel Arthur Phayre chief administrator of Bassein and also charged him as envoy to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mindon imprisoned the king and seized the throne, sending envoys to Dalhousie to demand Bassein's return; London appointed Colonel Arthur Phayre Bassein's administrator and envoy in reply.

sentences.zh: 偕雅實勿裏行者為參贊亨利幼兒、地質學家倭爾罕，挾緬王立永讓擺古之約，緬王拒焉。

translations.literal: Those traveling with Arthur Phayre were the counselor Henry Yule and the geologist Oldham, bearing the Burmese king's treaty of perpetual cession of Bassein; the Burmese king refused.
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Henry Yule and geologist Oldham accompanied Phayre, bearing a treaty for Bassein's permanent cession; the king refused.

sentences.zh: 久之，至同治元年始定約，英乃於緬甸海岸設官分部，稱「英領緬甸」，即擺古、厄勒瓦諦、阿拉幹、地那悉林也。

translations.literal: After a long time, in the first year of Tongzhi the treaty was finally settled; Britain then established officials and subdivisions on the Burmese coast, calling it "British Burma"—that is, Bassein, Irrawaddy, Arakan, and Tenasserim.
translations.idiomatic: Years later, in Tongzhi year one, a treaty was signed; Britain organized the coast as "British Burma"—Bassein, Irrawaddy, Arakan, and Tenasserim.

sentences.zh: 以厄勒瓦諦江東支海口為會城，即所謂仰光鎮，以溫個那職視巡撫。

translations.literal: The estuary of the eastern branch of the Irrawaddy River was made the seat of government—that is, the so-called Rangoon garrison; Wen-gena held office equivalent to governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: The eastern Irrawaddy estuary became the seat of government—Rangoon—with Wen-gena serving in a role akin to governor-general.

sentences.zh: 初，英人欲覓一自英領緬甸通中國商路，苦為緬隔。

translations.literal: At first the British wished to find a trade route from British Burma to China, but were troubled that Burma lay in between.
translations.idiomatic: Britain first sought a trade route from British Burma to China, blocked by Burmese territory.

sentences.zh: 後緬王許英人威廉遊歷緬境，北抵八募，又溯厄勒瓦諦江而上，至江上游之山峽。

translations.literal: Later the Burmese king permitted the Englishman Williams to travel through Burmese territory, reaching Bhamo in the north, and also going up the Irrawaddy River to the mountain gorges of the upper river.
translations.idiomatic: Later the king allowed Williams to traverse Burma north to Bhamo and up the Irrawaddy to its upper gorges.

sentences.zh: 同治六年，緬廷與英人結通航緬境之約，又命英人代收八募與其他口岸商稅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tongzhi the Burmese court concluded a treaty with the British on navigation within Burmese territory, and also ordered the British to collect commercial taxes at Bhamo and other ports on their behalf.
translations.idiomatic: In Tongzhi year six Burma granted navigation rights and entrusted Bhamo and other port duties to British collection.

sentences.zh: 次年，緬王曼同薨，子錫袍嗣位，復命旅於仰光之英工程師威廉、生物理學學士愛迭生、水師兵官暴厄爾與司忒華德、白恩諸人探訪運路，而以軍佐斯賴登率之行，且諭八募守臣以兵五十人護行。

translations.literal: The next year King Mindon died and his son Thibaw succeeded; he again ordered the British engineer Williams stationed at Rangoon, Bachelor of Science Edison, naval officers Bourne and Stewart, and Bai-en and others to explore transport routes, with Colonel Sladen leading the expedition, and also instructed the Bhamo garrison commander to provide fifty soldiers as escort.
translations.idiomatic: The next year Mindon died and Thibaw succeeded; he again dispatched Williams the engineer, Edison the scientist, naval officers Bourne and Stewart, Bai-en, and others under Colonel Sladen to survey routes, with fifty Bhamo troops as escort.

sentences.zh: 於是安抵八募東北之中國騰越廳境。

translations.literal: They thus safely reached the border of China's Tengyue sub-prefecture northeast of Bhamo.
translations.idiomatic: They reached China's Tengyue sub-prefecture northeast of Bhamo without incident.

sentences.zh: 八年，緬始開厄勒瓦諦江航路，上通八募，命水師兵官斯討拉爾駐八募，理其事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Burma first opened the Irrawaddy River route, reaching Bhamo upstream; a naval officer Storer was stationed at Bhamo to manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Burma opened the Irrawaddy to Bhamo; naval officer Storer was posted there to oversee navigation.

sentences.zh: 緬王頗注重商務，凡克亨山一帶危險地，皆設官防護，英人交口譽之。

translations.literal: The Burmese king paid considerable attention to commerce; all dangerous places along the Kaung-hin mountain range had officials set to protect travelers, and the British unanimously praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The king valued commerce, posting guards along the perilous Kaung-hin route—earning universal British praise.

sentences.zh: 然緬王戇而多忌，廢斥舊臣，誅鋤兄弟親戚殆盡。

translations.literal: Yet the Burmese king was obtuse and suspicious in the extreme; he dismissed old ministers and executed or eliminated brothers and kinsmen almost to the last.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the king was dull and deeply suspicious, purging old ministers and slaughtering kinsmen nearly to extinction.

sentences.zh: 外官雖有四千六百餘土司，皆祿無常俸，專朘民膏，百姓恆產，任意抄沒，緬、英雖交好，而猜忌尤深。

translations.literal: Although there were more than four thousand six hundred local headmen outside the capital, all without fixed salaries, they exclusively drained the people's substance; the people's constant property was arbitrarily confiscated; although Burma and Britain were on good terms, suspicion ran especially deep.
translations.idiomatic: More than four thousand six hundred unsalaried frontier headmen preyed on the people, seizing property at will; despite outward friendship with Britain, mutual suspicion ran deep.

sentences.zh: 光緒九年，法蘭西由下安南進踞北圻，暹羅亦命官分駐老撾土酋各部，英據南緬既久，洞知上緬寶藏之區，甲於南海，且慮法人由北圻西趨，蔓及緬甸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Guangxu, France advanced from lower Annam to occupy Tonkin; Siam also ordered officials to be stationed at the various Lao chieftaincies; Britain had long held southern Burma and knew well that upper Burma's treasure regions surpassed those of the South Sea, and also feared the French might advance west from Tonkin and spread to Burma.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangxu year nine France seized Tonkin from lower Annam; Siam posted officials across Laos; long established in the south, Britain coveted upper Burma's riches and feared French expansion westward from Tonkin.

sentences.zh: 十一年十月三日，英首相侯爵沙力斯伯裏值倫敦府尹大宴時，宣佈伐緬意，假判斷木商歇業為名，由印度派兵進攻，入蠻得勒，擒其王，流之於印度孟買海濱拉德乃奇黎島。

translations.literal: On the third day of the tenth month of the eleventh year, at a great banquet of the Lord Mayor of London, the British Prime Minister the Marquess of Salisbury announced the intention to attack Burma, using as pretext the judgment of a timber merchant's business suspension; troops were dispatched from India to attack, entering Mandalay, capturing its king, and exiling him to Ratnagiri Island on the Bombay coast of India.
translations.idiomatic: On the tenth month's third day in year eleven, at the Lord Mayor's banquet, Prime Minister Salisbury announced war on Burma over a timber merchant's dispute; Indian troops took Mandalay, captured the king, and exiled him to Ratnagiri off Bombay.

sentences.zh: 初，緬與法蘭西、義大利立私約，損自主權利，英弗善也。

translations.literal: Earlier Burma had made private treaties with France and Italy, impairing its sovereign rights; Britain was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Burma had earlier signed private treaties with France and Italy that eroded its sovereignty—London was displeased.

sentences.zh: 至是欲存緬祀，則私約不能廢，遂決計滅之，並取所屬拈人地。

translations.literal: By then, to preserve Burma's sacrificial rites the private treaties could not be abolished; they therefore resolved to destroy it and also take the Nian people's lands under its authority.
translations.idiomatic: To preserve the dynasty required keeping those treaties; Britain therefore resolved to annex Burma and its Nian dependencies.

sentences.zh: 南緬地區部為四：曰擺古部，曰阿拉幹部，曰厄勒瓦諦部，曰地那悉林部。

translations.literal: The southern Burma region was divided into four departments: Bassein, Arakan, Irrawaddy, and Tenasserim.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Burma was divided into four departments: Bassein, Arakan, Irrawaddy, and Tenasserim.

sentences.zh: 北緬地區部為六：曰北部，曰中部，曰拉歇山嶺部，曰南部，曰東部，曰喀倫尼山嶺部，各部皆設行政長官，而隸於印度總督，緬甸自是遂亡。

translations.literal: The northern Burma region was divided into six departments: the north, the center, the Yoma mountain range, the south, the east, and the Karenni mountain range; each department had a chief administrator subordinate to the Governor-General of India; Burma was thus extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Burma comprised six departments—north, center, Yoma hills, south, east, and Karenni hills—each under an administrator reporting to India's Governor-General; Burma ceased to exist.

sentences.zh: 時出使大臣曾紀澤駐英，帝以屬國故，命與英外部會商緬事。

translations.literal: At the time the envoy-minister Zeng Jize was stationed in Britain; because it was a dependent state, the Emperor ordered him to consult with the British Foreign Office on Burmese affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Envoy Zeng Jize was then in London; the Emperor ordered him to consult the Foreign Office because Burma was a tributary state.

sentences.zh: 初議立君存祀，俾守十年一貢之例，不可得。

translations.literal: At first they discussed installing a ruler to preserve sacrificial rites and maintain the ten-year tribute precedent; this could not be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: They first proposed preserving the dynasty and ten-year tribute schedule—Britain refused.

sentences.zh: 旋議由英駐緬大員按期遣使齎送儀物，其界務、商務兩事，則擬先定分界，再議通商。

translations.literal: Soon they discussed having the British chief in Burma dispatch envoys on schedule bearing ceremonial gifts; as for boundary and commercial affairs, they proposed first fixing the boundary and then discussing trade.
translations.idiomatic: Talk turned to British envoys bearing tribute gifts on schedule; boundary and trade were to be settled separately—boundaries first, commerce later.

sentences.zh: 英人自以驟辟緬甸全境，所獲已多，有稍讓中國展拓邊界之意。

translations.literal: The British themselves, having suddenly opened all of Burma and gained much, had some intention of slightly yielding to China in extending the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Having seized all Burma at a stroke, the British were somewhat willing to let China expand its frontier.

sentences.zh: 英外部侍郎克蕾稱：「英廷原將潞江以東之地，自雲南南界之外起，南抵暹羅北界，西濱潞江，即洋圖所謂薩爾溫江，東抵瀾滄江下游，其中北有南掌國，南有拈人各種，或留為屬國，或收為屬地，聽中國自裁。」

translations.literal: The British Under-Secretary Clare stated: "The British court originally intended the lands east of the Lu River, beginning outside Yunnan's southern border, south to Siam's northern border, west bordering the Lu River—that is, the Salween on foreign maps—east reaching the lower reaches of the Lancang River; within this region the north has the state of Lan Xang and the south has the various Nian peoples; whether to leave them as dependent states or take them as dependent territory is for China to decide."
translations.idiomatic: Under-Secretary Clare said: "Britain would yield lands east of the Lu River—from beyond Yunnan's southern border south to Siam, west to the Salween, east to the lower Mekong—including Lan Xang in the north and Nian peoples in the south; China might keep them as tributaries or annex them as territory."

sentences.zh: 曾紀澤轉咨總理衙門，言：「南掌本中華貢國，英人果將潞江以東讓我，宜即受之，將拈人、南掌均留為屬國，責其按期朝貢，並將上邦之權明告天下，方可防後患而固邊圉。」

translations.literal: Zeng Jize forwarded inquiry to the Zongli Yamen, saying: "Lan Xang was originally a tributary state of China; if the British truly yield the lands east of the Lu River, we should accept them at once, leave the Nian people and Lan Xang as dependent states, charge them with periodic tribute to court, and clearly announce the suzerain's authority to the world—only then can later troubles be prevented and the frontier secured."
translations.idiomatic: Zeng reported to the Zongli Yamen: "Lan Xang was China's tributary; if Britain truly ceded land east of the Lu River, we should accept, keep the Nian peoples and Lan Xang as dependencies under tribute, and proclaim suzerainty to the world—securing the frontier against future trouble."

sentences.zh: 紀澤又向英外部索還八募。

translations.literal: Zeng Jize also demanded the return of Bhamo from the British Foreign Office.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng also demanded Bhamo's return.

sentences.zh: 八募即蠻幕之新街。

translations.literal: Bhamo is the Xinjie of Manmu.
translations.idiomatic: Bhamo is Xinjie of the Manmu domain.

sentences.zh: 昔時蠻幕土司地甚大，後悉並於緬，其商貨彙集之區謂之新街，洋圖譯音則為八募，距騰越邊外百數十里，在大金沙江上游之東，龍川江下游之北，檳榔江下游之南，向為滇、緬通商巨鎮。

translations.literal: Formerly the Manmu chieftain's territory was very large; later it was entirely annexed by Burma; the district where goods gathered was called Xinjie, which foreign maps transliterated as Bhamo; it lay over a hundred li beyond the Tengyue border, east of the upper Irrawaddy, north of the lower Longchuan River, south of the lower Betel-nut River, and had long been a great entrepot of trade between Yunnan and Burma.
translations.idiomatic: Once vast, the Manmu domain was absorbed by Burma; its trading center Xinjie—Bhamo on foreign maps—lay a hundred-odd li beyond Tengyue, east of the upper Irrawaddy between the Longchuan and Betel-nut rivers—a major Yunnan-Burma mart.

sentences.zh: 英人以其為全緬菁華所萃，不許。

translations.literal: The British, because it was where all the choicest goods of Burma gathered, would not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: Britain refused—it was the jewel of all Burma's commerce.

sentences.zh: 爭論久之，克蕾始雲，英廷已飭駐緬英官勘驗一地，以便允中國立埠，且可在彼設關收稅。

translations.literal: After long dispute Clare finally said the British court had ordered the British official in Burma to survey a site so as to permit China to establish a trading port, and customs could also be collected there.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged debate Clare said Britain would survey a site for a Chinese trading port with customs rights.

sentences.zh: 參贊官馬格裏言八募雖不可得，其東二三十里舊有八募城，似肯讓與中國，日後貿易亦可大興。

translations.literal: Counselor Mark said that although Bhamo could not be obtained, some twenty or thirty li to its east was the old Bhamo city, which seemed willing to be yielded to China; trade could flourish greatly there in future.
translations.idiomatic: Counselor Mark noted Bhamo itself was unobtainable, but old Bhamo city twenty or thirty li east might be ceded—with great trade potential.

sentences.zh: 且允將大金沙江為兩國公共之江，如此，則利益與彼分之，其隱裨大局，尤較得潞東之地為勝。

translations.literal: They also agreed to make the great Irrawaddy a river common to both countries; thus the benefits would be shared with them, and the hidden benefit to the overall situation would be even better than obtaining the lands east of the Lu River.
translations.idiomatic: They also offered joint use of the Irrawaddy—sharing benefits more advantageously, they argued, than taking land east of the Lu River.

sentences.zh: 議未定，紀澤旋回國。

translations.literal: The negotiations were unsettled when Zeng Jize soon returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Talks remained inconclusive when Zeng returned home.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月，總署與英使歐格訥議約五條：第一，申明十年呈進方物之例；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twelfth year the Zongli Yamen negotiated five articles of treaty with the British envoy O'Conor: first, reaffirm the precedent of presenting tribute gifts every ten years;
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of year twelve the Zongli Yamen and envoy O'Conor agreed on five treaty articles: first, reaffirm the ten-year tribute schedule;

sentences.zh: 第三，中緬邊界應由中、英兩國派員會同勘定，其邊界通商事宜另立專章。

translations.literal: Third, the Sino-Burmese boundary should be jointly surveyed by Chinese and British commissioners; border trade matters would be set forth in a separate chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Third, the Sino-Burmese border would be jointly surveyed, with trade provisions in a separate chapter.

sentences.zh: 約成，遷延者五年。

translations.literal: When the treaty was concluded, delay lasted five years.
translations.idiomatic: The treaty signed, implementation stalled for five years.

sentences.zh: 十七年，出使大臣薛福成始申前議，奏言：「英人所稱原讓潞東之地，南北將及千里，東西亦五六百里，果能將南掌與拈人收為屬國，或列為甌脫之地，誠系綏邊保小之良圖。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the envoy-minister Xue Fucheng raised the earlier proposal, memorializing: "The lands east of the Lu River that the British said they would originally yield extend nearly a thousand li north to south and five or six hundred li east to west; if the Nian people and Lan Xang can truly be taken as dependent states or listed as buffer territory, this is indeed an excellent plan for securing the frontier and protecting small states.
translations.idiomatic: In year seventeen Envoy Xue Fucheng revived the proposal: "The Lu River east lands Britain once offered span nearly a thousand li north-south and five or six hundred east-west; keeping the Nian peoples and Lan Xang as dependencies or buffer zones would truly secure the frontier.

sentences.zh: 惟查南掌即老撾之轉音。

translations.literal: Yet upon examination Lan Xang is a transliteration of Laos.
translations.idiomatic: But Lan Xang is simply Laos transliterated.

sentences.zh: 臣閱外洋最新圖說，似老撾已歸屬暹羅。

translations.literal: Your servant has read the latest foreign maps and gazetteers, which seem to show Laos already subordinate to Siam.
translations.idiomatic: Latest foreign maps suggest Laos already belongs to Siam.

sentences.zh: 若徒受英人之虛惠，終不能實有其地，非計之得者。

translations.literal: If we merely accept the British empty favor, in the end we cannot truly possess the land—this is not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting an empty British concession would gain us nothing—a poor bargain.

sentences.zh: 南掌、拈人本各判為數小國，分附緬甸、暹羅。

translations.literal: The Nian people and Lan Xang were originally each divided into several small states, separately attached to Burma and Siam.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian peoples and Lan Xang were fragmented small states owing allegiance variously to Burma and Siam.

sentences.zh: 宜先查明南掌入暹羅之外，是否尚有自立之國，以定受與不受。

translations.literal: We should first ascertain whether, apart from Lan Xang's incorporation into Siam, any independent states still remain, to decide whether to accept or not.
translations.idiomatic: We must first determine whether any independent states remain besides Laos under Siam before deciding to accept.

sentences.zh: 其向附緬甸之拈人，地實大於南掌，稍能自立，且素服中國之化。

translations.literal: The Nian people formerly attached to Burma occupy territory actually larger than Lan Xang, are somewhat able to stand independently, and have long been receptive to Chinese civilization.
translations.idiomatic: The Burma-leaning Nian peoples hold more land than Lan Xang, maintain some independence, and have long accepted Chinese culture.

sentences.zh: 若收為我屬，則普洱、順甯等府邊徼皆可鞏固矣。

translations.literal: If taken as our dependencies, the frontiers of Pu'er, Shunning, and other prefectures can all be secured.
translations.idiomatic: If brought under our suzerainty, Pu'er, Shunning, and neighboring frontiers would be secured.

sentences.zh: 至曾紀澤所索八募之地，雖為英人所不肯舍，其曾經默許之舊八募者，亦可為通至大金沙江張本。

translations.literal: As for the Bhamo territory Zeng Jize demanded, although the British were unwilling to relinquish it, the old Bhamo they once tacitly permitted could still serve as a basis for extending trade to the great Irrawaddy.
translations.idiomatic: Bhamo itself Britain would not yield—but the old Bhamo once tacitly offered could anchor trade access to the Irrawaddy.

sentences.zh: 若將來竟不與爭，或爭而不得，竊有五慮焉。

translations.literal: If in future we ultimately do not contest it, or contest and fail to obtain it, your servant privately has five concerns.
translations.idiomatic: If we fail to contest Bhamo—or contest and lose—I have five private concerns.

sentences.zh: 夫天下事不進則退。

translations.literal: Affairs under Heaven advance or retreat; there is no standing still.
translations.idiomatic: In affairs of state, one advances or retreats—never stands still.

sentences.zh: 從前展拓邊界之論，非謂足增中國之大也。

translations.literal: The earlier talk of extending the frontier was not meant to say it would suffice to enlarge China's size.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier extension was never merely about enlarging China's map.

sentences.zh: 臣聞乾隆年間，緬甸恃強不靖，吞滅滇邊諸土司，騰越八關之外，形勢不全。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that in the Qianlong period Burma relied on its strength and was unruly, swallowing and extinguishing the various tribal headmen on Yunnan's border; beyond Tengyue's eight passes the strategic situation was incomplete.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianlong era Burma's strength swallowed Yunnan frontier headmen; beyond Tengyue's eight passes the strategic position was incomplete.

sentences.zh: 西南一隅，本多不甚清晰之界，若我不求展出，彼或反將勘入。

translations.literal: The southwest corner originally had many boundaries not very clearly defined; if we do not seek to extend outward, they may instead survey inward.
translations.idiomatic: The southwest had many ill-defined borders; if we do not push outward, others may survey inward.

sentences.zh: 一慮也。

translations.literal: This is the first concern.
translations.idiomatic: That is the first concern.

sentences.zh: 我不於邊外稍留餘地，彼必築鐵路直接滇邊，一遇有事，動受要脅。

translations.literal: If we do not leave a little margin beyond the border, they will certainly build a railway directly to the Yunnan frontier; whenever trouble arises, we will constantly be subject to coercion.
translations.idiomatic: If we leave no buffer beyond the frontier, they will run a railway straight to Yunnan's border—and whenever crisis comes, we will be at their mercy.

sentences.zh: 二慮也。

translations.literal: This is the second concern.
translations.idiomatic: That is the second concern.

sentences.zh: 長江上源為小金沙江，最上之源由藏入滇，距邊甚近，洋圖即謂之揚子江。

translations.literal: The upper reaches of the Yangtze River are the Jinsha River; its highest source enters Yunnan from Tibet, very close to the border; on foreign maps it is called the Yangtze River.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze's upper reach is the Jinsha River, whose Tibetan headwaters enter Yunnan near the border—foreign maps simply call it the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 我若進分大金沙江之利，尚可使彼離邊稍遠。

translations.literal: If we advance to share in the benefits of the great Irrawaddy, we can still keep them somewhat farther from the border.
translations.idiomatic: By securing a share of the Irrawaddy's benefits, we might still keep them farther from the frontier.

sentences.zh: 萬一能守故界，則彼窺知江源伊邇，或浸圖行船，徑入長江以爭通商之利。

translations.literal: If by chance we can hold the old boundary, they will spy and learn how close the river's source is, and may gradually scheme to navigate ships directly into the Yangtze to compete for commercial benefits.
translations.idiomatic: If we merely hold the old line, they will discover how near the river's source lies—and may gradually aim to sail into the Yangtze and seize trade advantages.

sentences.zh: 三慮也。

translations.literal: This is the third concern.
translations.idiomatic: That is the third concern.

sentences.zh: 夫英人經營商埠，是其長技。

translations.literal: Managing commercial ports is the British forte.
translations.idiomatic: Building trade ports is Britain's specialty.

sentences.zh: 我稍展界，則通商在緬甸，設關收稅，亦可與之俱旺。

translations.literal: If we extend the boundary slightly, trade will be in Burma; we can establish customs posts and collect taxes, and prosperity can grow along with theirs.
translations.idiomatic: A modest border extension would keep trade in Burma, where we could levy customs and prosper alongside them.

sentences.zh: 我不展界，則通商在滇境，將來彼且來擇租界、設領事，地方諸務不能不受其牽制。

translations.literal: If we do not extend the boundary, trade will be in Yunnan territory; in future they will come to choose concessions and establish consuls, and local affairs cannot but be subject to their control.
translations.idiomatic: Without extension, trade falls within Yunnan—and they will eventually demand concessions and consuls, constraining local governance.

sentences.zh: 四慮也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth concern.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fourth concern.

sentences.zh: 我得大金沙江之利，則迤西一路之銅，可由輪船遵海北上，運費當省倍蓰。

translations.literal: If we gain the benefits of the great Irrawaddy, the copper of the western route can be shipped north by steamer along the sea, and transport costs should be reduced several times over.
translations.idiomatic: Control of the Irrawaddy would let western Yunnan's copper go north by sea steamer—cutting transport costs many times over.

sentences.zh: 否則彼獨據運貨之利，既入滇境，窺知礦產之富，或且漸生狡謀。

translations.literal: Otherwise they alone will monopolize the benefit of transport; having entered Yunnan territory, they will spy and learn how rich the mineral resources are, and may gradually hatch crafty schemes.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise they alone would control shipping; once inside Yunnan they would learn how rich the mines are—and crafty designs might follow.

sentences.zh: 五慮也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth concern.
translations.idiomatic: That is the fifth concern.

sentences.zh: 凡此五慮，皆在意計之中。

translations.literal: All these five concerns are within deliberate calculation.
translations.idiomatic: All five concerns were carefully weighed.

sentences.zh: 又查中、英所定緬約第一條內，緬甸每屆十年，向有派員呈進方物成例。

translations.literal: Further inquiry shows that within the first article of the Sino-British Burmese treaty, there was an established precedent of Burma every ten years dispatching envoys to present tribute gifts.
translations.idiomatic: The first article of the Sino-British Burma treaty also reaffirmed Burma's ten-year tribute precedent.

sentences.zh: 英國允由緬甸最大之大臣，每屆十年派員循例舉行，所派之人應選緬甸國人等語。

translations.literal: Britain agreed that Burma's senior minister would every ten years dispatch envoys according to precedent, and the persons dispatched should be chosen from among Burmese nationals, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Britain agreed that every ten years Burma's chief minister would send Burmese envoys bearing tribute as before.

sentences.zh: 當時中外注意專在申明成例，惟緬甸何年入貢，並未計及，所以但有此約，而英之駐緬大員尚未舉行。

translations.literal: At the time Chinese and foreign attention focused solely on reaffirming the precedent; which year Burma should send tribute was not considered, so although this treaty existed, the British chief in Burma had not yet carried it out.
translations.idiomatic: Attention then focused only on reaffirming precedent—not on which year Burma last sent tribute; so though the treaty stood, Britain's resident in Burma had not acted.

sentences.zh: 竊恐久不催問，此約即成虛設。

translations.literal: I fear that if not pressed for long, this treaty provision will become empty form.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that without prompt inquiry this clause will lapse into a dead letter.

sentences.zh: 臣查成案，緬甸向系十年一貢。

translations.literal: Your servant has examined precedent: Burma has always submitted tribute once every ten years.
translations.idiomatic: Precedent shows Burma paid tribute every ten years.

sentences.zh: 自道光二十三年入貢後，道路不通，至光緒元年始復入貢一次。

translations.literal: After tribute in the twenty-third year of Daoguang, the route was blocked; not until the first year of Guangxu was tribute sent once again.
translations.idiomatic: After Daoguang year twenty-three the route was cut off; tribute resumed only once, in Guangxu year one.

sentences.zh: 計截至光緒十一年，正應緬甸入貢之期。

translations.literal: Calculating to Guangxu year eleven, it was precisely the period when Burma should have sent tribute.
translations.idiomatic: By Guangxu year eleven Burma's tribute year had come due.

sentences.zh: 若不按時理論，彼亦斷不過問。

translations.literal: If we do not raise the matter on schedule, they certainly will not inquire either.
translations.idiomatic: If we do not raise it on schedule, Britain will certainly not raise it either.

sentences.zh: 此與勘界各為一事，未便受其牽制，臣擬再加查訪，即行文外部，請其知照駐緬大員，補進光緒十一年應呈方物，俟光緒二十一年，再按定例辦理。

translations.literal: This and boundary demarcation are separate matters and should not be held hostage to each other; your servant proposes further inquiry and to write the Foreign Office, requesting notification to the British chief in Burma to make up the tribute gifts due in Guangxu year eleven, and then in Guangxu year twenty-one to proceed according to the fixed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Boundary work and tribute are separate and should not be linked; I propose further inquiry and a note to the Foreign Office asking Britain's resident in Burma to deliver the Guangxu year eleven tribute, then resume the regular schedule in Guangxu year twenty-one.

sentences.zh: 萬一彼謂必俟駐緬十年始呈方物，則經此一番考覈，彼於光緒二十一年之期斷難宕緩矣。」

translations.literal: If they should say tribute gifts must wait until ten years after the resident arrives in Burma, then after this round of examination they will find it hard to delay the Guangxu year twenty-one deadline."
translations.idiomatic: If they claim tribute must wait ten years from the resident's arrival, this inquiry will at least make them honor the Guangxu year twenty-one deadline."

sentences.zh: 既而英人不認允曾紀澤三端之說，謂普洱外邊南掌、拈人諸地，及大金沙江為公用之江，與八募設關也。

translations.literal: Subsequently the British refused to accept Zeng Jize's three proposals, regarding the lands of Lan Xang and the Nian peoples beyond Pu'er, the great Irrawaddy as a common river, and customs at Bhamo.
translations.idiomatic: Britain then rejected Zeng Jize's three proposals—Lan Xang and Nian lands beyond Pu'er, joint use of the Irrawaddy, and a customs post at Bhamo.

sentences.zh: 十九年七月，福成奏言：「英人自翻前議，雖以公法為解，實亦時勢使然。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the nineteenth year Fucheng memorialized: "The British have reversed their earlier proposals; although they cite international law, in truth the times have compelled it.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year nineteen Xue Fucheng memorialized: "Britain has reversed its earlier offers—citing international law, but really yielding to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 前議三端，既不可恃，則展拓邊界之舉，毫無把握。

translations.literal: The three earlier proposals can no longer be relied upon; the effort to extend the frontier is entirely without assurance.
translations.idiomatic: Those three earlier offers are gone; any hope of extending the frontier has vanished.

sentences.zh: 前歲英兵遊弋滇邊，以查界為名，闌入界內。

translations.literal: The year before last British troops patrolled the Yunnan border, and under the pretext of surveying the boundary intruded within the line.
translations.idiomatic: Two years earlier British troops had patrolled Yunnan's border and, under cover of boundary survey, crossed the line.

sentences.zh: 常駐之地，則有神護關外之昔董，暨鐵壁關外之漢董。

translations.literal: Places where they were permanently stationed included Hsihkyeng beyond the Shenhu Pass and Hsihkhu beyond the Iron Wall Pass.
translations.idiomatic: They had established permanent posts at Hsihkyeng beyond Shenhu Pass and Hsihkhu beyond Iron Wall Pass.

sentences.zh: 雲貴督臣王文韶迭經電達總理衙門。

translations.literal: The Yunnan-Guizhou governor Wang Wenshao repeatedly telegraphed the Zongli Yamen.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Wenshao of Yunnan-Guizhou telegraphed the Zongli Yamen repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 臣承總理衙門急電，照會外部，斥其違理，責令退兵。

translations.literal: Your servant, on urgent telegram from the Zongli Yamen, presented a note to the Foreign Office, rebuking their violation of principle and demanding withdrawal of troops.
translations.idiomatic: On urgent orders from the Zongli Yamen I protested to the Foreign Office, condemning the violation and demanding withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 又屢赴外部爭論，英兵稍自撤退，滇邊至今靜謐。

translations.literal: I also repeatedly went to the Foreign Office to argue; the British troops gradually withdrew of themselves, and the Yunnan border has remained quiet to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated protests at the Foreign Office gradually brought withdrawal; the Yunnan frontier has been quiet since.

sentences.zh: 臣又查野人山地，綿亙數千里，不在緬甸轄境之內。

translations.literal: Your servant also found that the Wild Headman Hills stretch for several thousand li and lie outside Burmese jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: I also found that the Wild Headman Hills stretch thousands of li beyond Burma's jurisdiction.

sentences.zh: 曾紀澤曾照會外部，請以大金沙江為界，江東之境，均歸滇屬，英人堅拒不納。

translations.literal: Zeng Jize once presented a note to the Foreign Office requesting the great Irrawaddy as boundary, with all lands east of the river under Yunnan; the British firmly refused.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Jize had proposed the Irrawaddy as boundary, with all lands east under Yunnan—Britain refused.

sentences.zh: 其印督至進兵盞達邊外之昔馬，攻擊野人，以示不原分地之意。

translations.literal: The Governor-General of India even sent troops to Hsima beyond the border of Chendu to attack the hill tribes, showing unwillingness to cede territory.
translations.idiomatic: India's Governor-General even marched to Hsima beyond Chendu and attacked hill tribes to show he would not yield territory.

sentences.zh: 臣相機理論，稍就範圍，於是有就滇境東南讓我稍展邊界之說。

translations.literal: Your servant argued as opportunity allowed and gradually brought them into bounds; thereupon arose talk of Britain yielding a slight frontier extension on Yunnan's southeast.
translations.idiomatic: I negotiated as circumstances allowed and gradually narrowed the dispute—until talk arose of a modest extension on Yunnan's southeast.

sentences.zh: 據稱已與印督商定於孟定橄欖壩西南邊外讓我一地曰科幹，在南丁河與潞河中間，蓋即孟艮土司舊壤，計七百五十英方里。

translations.literal: It was reported that agreement had been reached with the Governor-General to yield China a place called Kogan southwest beyond Mengding Olive Dam, between the Namting and Lu rivers—essentially the old domain of the Menggen chieftain—totaling seven hundred fifty square English miles.
translations.idiomatic: Reportedly Britain agreed to cede Kogan southwest of Mengding Olive Dam, between the Namting and Lu rivers—the old Menggen chieftaincy—some seven hundred fifty square miles.

sentences.zh: 又自孟卯土司邊外包括漢龍關在內，作一直線，東抵潞江麻栗壩之對岸止，悉劃歸中國，約計八百英方里。

translations.literal: Further, from beyond the Mengmao chieftain's border including Hanlong Pass, drawing a straight line east to the opposite bank of Maliba on the Lu River—all to be assigned to China—totaling about eight hundred square English miles.
translations.idiomatic: From beyond the Mengmao chieftaincy, including Hanlong Pass, a straight line east to the Lu River's Maliba bank would also go to China—about eight hundred square miles.

sentences.zh: 又有車裏、孟連土司，轄境甚廣，向隸雲南版圖，近有新設鎮邊一廳，系從孟連屬境分出。

translations.literal: There were also the Cheli and Menglian chieftains, whose jurisdictions were very broad, formerly under Yunnan's dominion; recently a Zhenbian sub-prefecture had been newly established, split from Menglian's dependent territory.
translations.idiomatic: The Cheli and Menglian chieftaincies—once broad domains under Yunnan, recently split to form Zhenbian sub-prefecture—were also involved.

sentences.zh: 英人以兩土司昔嘗入貢於緬，並此一廳爭為兩屬，今亦原以全權讓我，訂定約章，永不過問。

translations.literal: The British, because the two chieftains had once sent tribute to Burma, disputed them and the sub-prefecture as dual dependencies; now they also agreed to yield full authority to us, fixing it by treaty and never again interfering.
translations.idiomatic: Britain had claimed dual suzerainty because both chieftains once tribute Burma—but now agreed to cede full authority by treaty, never to interfere again.

sentences.zh: 至滇西老界與野人山地毗連之處，亦允我酌量展出。

translations.literal: As for places where Yunnan's old boundary adjoined the Wild Headman Hills, they also permitted us to extend outward as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Where Yunnan's old line met the Wild Headman Hills, they also allowed modest outward extension.

sentences.zh: 其駐兵之昔董大寨，雖未肯讓歸中國，原以穆雷江北現駐英兵之昔馬歸我，南起坪隴峰，北抵薩伯坪峰，西逾南嶂至新陌，計三百英方里；

translations.literal: Although they would not yield the great Hsihkyeng camp where troops were stationed to China, they agreed to give us Hsima north of the Mule River where British troops were now stationed—from Pinglong Peak south to Sabaping Peak north, west beyond Nanzhang to Xinmo—totaling three hundred square English miles;
translations.idiomatic: They would not yield the main Hsihkyeng garrison, but offered Hsima north of the Mule River—from Pinglong Peak south to Sabaping Peak north, west to Xinmo beyond Nanzhang—three hundred square miles;

sentences.zh: 又自穆雷江以南、既陽江以東有一地，約計七八十英方里。

translations.literal: Further, south of the Mule River and east of the Jiyang River there was a tract totaling about seventy or eighty square English miles.
translations.idiomatic: plus another seventy or eighty square miles south of the Mule River and east of the Jiyang River.

sentences.zh: 是彼於野人山地亦稍讓矣。

translations.literal: Thus they also yielded somewhat in the Wild Headman Hills.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they yielded ground even in the Wild Headman Hills.

sentences.zh: 其餘均依滇省原圖界線劃分。

translations.literal: The remainder was all divided according to Yunnan's original map boundary.
translations.idiomatic: The rest followed Yunnan's original map line.

sentences.zh: 外部於三月二十三日行文照會前來，臣先行文外部，訂定大局。

translations.literal: The Foreign Office on the twenty-third day of the third month sent a note; your servant first wrote the Foreign Office to settle the overall arrangement.
translations.idiomatic: On the third month's twenty-third day the Foreign Office sent a note; I had already written to settle the broad terms.

sentences.zh: 惟騰越八關界趾未清，尚須理論。

translations.literal: Only the boundaries of Tengyue's eight passes were not yet clear and still required negotiation.
translations.idiomatic: Only Tengyue's eight passes remained unsettled.

sentences.zh: 外部請待印督所寄地圖，又值外部諸員避暑在外，稍有停頓。

translations.literal: The Foreign Office asked to wait for maps sent by the Governor-General of India; moreover several Foreign Office staff were away on summer holiday, causing some delay.
translations.idiomatic: The Foreign Office awaited maps from India—and several officials were on summer holiday, causing delay.

sentences.zh: 前據督臣王文韶電稱漢龍關自前明已淪於緬，天馬關亦久為野人所占踞，則八關僅存六關。

translations.literal: Earlier Governor Wang Wenshao telegraphed that Hanlong Pass had fallen to Burma since the Ming, and Tianma Pass had long been occupied by hill tribes—so of the eight passes only six remained.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Wang Wenshao had reported that Hanlong Pass fell to Burma in the Ming and Tianma Pass to hill tribes—leaving only six of the eight passes.

sentences.zh: 現經再三爭論，此二關亦可歸中國。

translations.literal: After repeated argument, these two passes can also revert to China.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated argument both passes can revert to China.

sentences.zh: 又前年英兵所駐之漢董，本在界線之外，因其扼我形勢，逼處堪虞，向彼力索。

translations.literal: Further, Hsihkhu where British troops were stationed the year before last lay originally outside the boundary line; because it dominated our strategic position and its proximity was worrisome, we strongly demanded it from them.
translations.idiomatic: Hsihkhu, where British troops had camped, lay outside the line—but dominated our position; we pressed hard for its return.

sentences.zh: 外部亦原退讓，以表格外睦誼。

translations.literal: The Foreign Office also originally agreed to yield, to show exceptional cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: The Foreign Office agreed to yield it as a gesture of special goodwill.

sentences.zh: 刻下界務已竣，商務本不似界務之繁重，且已先將大意議明，無甚爭論。

translations.literal: At present boundary affairs are concluded; commercial affairs are not as burdensome as boundary affairs, and the main points have already been agreed with little dispute.
translations.idiomatic: Boundary work is now done; commerce is lighter work, and the main points are already agreed.

sentences.zh: 現正商訂條款，計可刻期蕆事。」

translations.literal: Articles are now being negotiated and should be completed on schedule."
translations.idiomatic: Treaty articles are being drafted and should be finished on schedule."

sentences.zh: 尋福成議定商約，續爭回鐵壁、虎踞二關，時二關皆英兵佔據也。

translations.literal: Soon Fucheng concluded the commercial treaty and further recovered the Iron Wall and Tiger Perch passes—both then occupied by British troops.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Fucheng soon concluded the commercial treaty and recovered Iron Wall and Tiger Perch passes—both held by British troops.

sentences.zh: 二十年正月，訂滇緬新約十九條，劃定自尖高山起，向西南行至江洪抵湄江之界線，大金沙江許中國任便行船，刪去八募設關一條。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twentieth year a new Yunnan-Burma treaty of nineteen articles was concluded, fixing the boundary from Jianshan Peak southwest to Chiang Hung reaching the Mekong River; the great Irrawaddy was permitted for China's free navigation; the article on customs at Bhamo was deleted.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year twenty a nineteen-article Yunnan-Burma treaty fixed the border from Jianshan Peak southwest to Chiang Hung on the Mekong, granted China free navigation on the Irrawaddy, and dropped the Bhamo customs clause.

sentences.zh: 於是緬事粗結。

translations.literal: Thereupon Burmese affairs were roughly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Burma affairs were thus roughly settled.

sentences.zh: 惟十年進呈方物之例，英外部初許待至光緒二十三年照約舉行；

translations.literal: Only the precedent of presenting tribute gifts every ten years—the British Foreign Office at first agreed to wait until Guangxu year twenty-three to carry it out according to treaty;
translations.idiomatic: Only the ten-year tribute precedent remained unsettled—the Foreign Office first agreed to wait until Guangxu year twenty-three;

sentences.zh: 繼稱英廷已豫備光緒二十年第一次派員赴中國，至是又聲請展緩，迄未實行云。

translations.literal: Then they said the British court had already prepared the first dispatch of envoys to China in Guangxu year twenty; by then they again requested postponement, and it has never been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: then said envoys would come in Guangxu year twenty—then asked delay again; it has never happened.

sentences.zh: 暹羅，在雲南之南，緬甸之東，越南之西，南瀕海灣。

translations.literal: Siam lies south of Yunnan, east of Burma, west of Vietnam, and borders the gulf to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Siam lay south of Yunnan, east of Burma, west of Vietnam, facing the gulf.

sentences.zh: 順治九年十二月，暹羅遣使請貢，並換給印、敕、勘合，允之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the ninth year of Shunzhi, Siam sent envoys requesting to send tribute and to have seals, patents, and tally-slips reissued; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Shunzhi year nine Siam asked to resume tribute and receive new seals, patents, and tally-slips—and was granted.

sentences.zh: 自是奉貢不絕。

translations.literal: From then on tribute was sent without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute then continued without interruption.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，暹羅正貢船行至七洲海面，遇風飄失護貢船一，至虎門，仍令駛回。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi, Siam's main tribute ship reached the Qizhou sea area; encountering wind, one escort tribute ship was lost; upon reaching Humen it was still ordered to sail back.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi year two Siam's main tribute ship reached the Qizhou seas; one escort was lost in a storm and, reaching Humen, was ordered to sail back.

sentences.zh: 三年七月，平南王尚可喜奏暹羅來餽禮物，卻不受。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the third year, Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi memorialized that Siam had sent gifts, which were declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year three Prince of Pingnan Shang Kexi reported Siam's gift offering, which was declined.

sentences.zh: 其年，議准暹羅進貢，正貢船二艘，員役二十名，補貢船一艘，員役六名，來京，並允貿易一次。

translations.literal: That year it was approved for Siam to send tribute: two main tribute ships with twenty personnel, one supplementary tribute ship with six personnel, coming to the capital, and one round of trade was also permitted.
translations.idiomatic: That year Siam's tribute was approved: two main ships with twenty men, one supplementary ship with six, bound for the capital—with one round of trade permitted.

sentences.zh: 明年十一月，國王遣陪臣等齎金葉表文，文曰：「暹羅國王臣森列拍臘照古龍拍臘馬嘑陸坤司由提呀菩埃誠惶誠恐稽首，謹奏大清皇帝陛下。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the next year the king dispatched accompanying ministers bearing a gold-leaf memorial, which read: "The King of Siam, your subject Sen Liet Phra Thaok Long Phra Ma Ha Lu Kun Si Yo Thia Pho Ae, with sincere fear and trembling kowtows, respectfully memorializes the Great Qing Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The next year's eleventh month the king sent ministers with a gold-leaf memorial: "The King of Siam, your subject Sen Liet Phra Thaok Long Phra Ma Ha Lu Kun Si Yo Thia Pho Ae, kowtows in fear and trembling to memorialize the Great Qing Emperor.

sentences.zh: 伏以新君禦世，普照中天，四海隸帡幪，萬方被教化。

translations.literal: Considering that the new ruler governs the age and illuminates the central heavens, the four seas are sheltered and the myriad regions receive civilization.
translations.idiomatic: The new Son of Heaven illuminates the realm; the four seas are sheltered and all lands receive civilization.

sentences.zh: 卑國久荷天恩，傾心葵藿，今特竭誠朝貢，敬差正貢使握坤司吝喇耶邁低禮、副貢使握坤心勿吞瓦替、三貢使握坤司敕博瓦綈、大通事揭帝典，辦事等臣，梯航渡海，齎上金葉表文、方物進獻，用伸拜舞之誠，恪盡遠臣之職。

translations.literal: Our humble state has long received Heaven's grace and turns its heart like the sunflower; now we specially exhaust sincerity in court tribute, respectfully dispatching chief tribute envoy Okun Si Lin Ya Mai Di Li, deputy tribute envoy Okun Sin Fotun Wati, third tribute envoy Okun Si Chi Bo Wati, chief interpreter Chai Di Dian, and ministerial officers and others, crossing seas by ladder-ship, bearing the gold-leaf memorial and local products to present, to express the sincerity of bowing and dancing, fully performing the duty of a distant subject.
translations.idiomatic: Our humble state long cherished Heaven's grace; now we send chief envoy Okun Si Lin Ya Mai Di Li, deputy Okun Sin Fotun Wati, third envoy Okun Si Chi Bo Wati, chief interpreter Chai Di Dian, and others across the seas with gold-leaf memorial and tribute gifts, bowing in distant loyalty.

sentences.zh: 伏冀俯垂天聽，寬宥不恭，微臣不勝瞻天仰聖戰慄屏營之至，謹具表以聞。

translations.literal: We humbly hope Your Majesty will incline Heaven's ear, pardon our lack of refinement; your humble subject cannot bear the awe of gazing toward Heaven and looking up to the Sage, trembling with apprehension—respectfully presenting this memorial to inform.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly beg Your Majesty to incline Heaven's ear and pardon our lack of refinement; trembling before Heaven and the Sage, we respectfully submit this memorial.

sentences.zh: 御前方物：龍涎香、西洋閃金緞、象牙、胡椒、腇黃、豆蔻、沉香、烏木、大楓子、金銀香、蘇木、孔雀、六足龜等；

translations.literal: Imperial gifts: ambergris, Western gold brocade, ivory, pepper, bezoar, cardamom, agarwood, ebony, large areca nuts, gold and silver incense, sappanwood, peacocks, six-legged tortoises, and so forth;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial gifts: ambergris, Western gold brocade, ivory, pepper, bezoar, cardamom, agarwood, ebony, areca nuts, gold and silver incense, sappanwood, peacocks, six-legged tortoises, and more;

sentences.zh: 皇后前半之。」

translations.literal: The Empress received half."
translations.idiomatic: The Empress received half."

sentences.zh: 帝錫國王緞、紗、羅各六；

translations.literal: The Emperor bestowed on the king six each of satin, gauze, and silk;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted the king six each of satin, gauze, and silk;

sentences.zh: 金緞、紗、羅各四，王妃各減二。

translations.literal: Four each of gold brocade, gauze, and silk; the queen consort received two fewer each.
translations.idiomatic: four each of gold brocade, gauze, and silk—the queen consort two fewer each.

sentences.zh: 正副使等賞賚有差。

translations.literal: The chief and deputy envoys and others received rewards in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Chief and deputy envoys received graded rewards.

sentences.zh: 定暹羅貢期三年一次，貢道由廣東，常貢外加貢無定額。

translations.literal: Siam's tribute schedule was fixed at once every three years, the tribute route through Guangdong; beyond regular tribute, supplementary tribute had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Siam's tribute was fixed at every three years via Guangdong; supplementary tribute had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 貢船以三艘為限，每艘不許逾百人，入京員役二十名，永以為例。

translations.literal: Tribute ships were limited to three; each ship was not permitted to exceed one hundred persons; personnel entering the capital were limited to twenty—forever established as precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute ships were capped at three, each under one hundred men, with twenty permitted in the capital—forever the rule.

sentences.zh: 十二年，貢使握坤司吝喇耶邁低禮等至，具表請封。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the tribute envoys Okun Si Lin Ya Mai Di Li and others arrived and submitted a memorial requesting investiture.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve envoys Okun Si Lin Ya Mai Di Li and others arrived requesting investiture.

sentences.zh: 四月，冊封暹羅國王，賜誥命及駝鈕鍍金銀印，令使臣齎回。

translations.literal: In the fourth month the King of Siam was invested and granted a patent of appointment and a camel-nobbed gilded silver seal, ordered the envoys to carry them back.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month the King of Siam was invested with patent and camel-nobbed gilded silver seal for the envoys to carry home.

sentences.zh: 誥曰：「來王來享，要荒昭事大之誠；

translations.literal: The patent read: "The king comes to enjoy—remote regions display sincerity in serving the great;
translations.idiomatic: The patent read: "The king comes to enjoy—in remote regions sincerity toward the great is shown;

sentences.zh: 悉主悉臣，國家著柔遠之義。

translations.literal: All subjects, all ministers—the state manifests the principle of gentle reach to the distant.
translations.idiomatic: all subjects, all ministers—the state shows its principle of gentle reach to the distant.

sentences.zh: 朕纘承鴻緒，期德教暨於遐陬，誕撫多方，使屏翰躋於康乂。

translations.literal: I continue the great enterprise, expecting virtue and teaching to reach the far corners, broadly cherishing the many regions, causing screen and rampart to ascend to peace and order.
translations.idiomatic: I continue the great enterprise, expecting virtue to reach the far corners, cherishing all regions until border and center alike know peace.

sentences.zh: 彝章具在，渙號宜頒。

translations.literal: The eternal statutes are in place; the proclamation should be issued.
translations.idiomatic: The eternal statutes stand; the proclamation should go forth.

sentences.zh: 爾暹羅國森烈拍臘照古龍拍臘馬嘑陸坤司由提呀菩埃秉志忠誠，服躬禮義，既傾心以向化，乃航海而請封。

translations.literal: You, King of Siam Sen Liet Phra Thaok Long Phra Ma Ha Lu Kun Si Yo Thia Pho Ae, hold loyal purpose and serve with ritual propriety; having turned your heart to civilization, you crossed the sea to request investiture.
translations.idiomatic: You, King of Siam Sen Liet Phra Thaok Long Phra Ma Ha Lu Kun Si Yo Thia Pho Ae, have held loyal purpose and served with propriety; having turned to civilization, you crossed the sea to request investiture.

sentences.zh: 礪山帶河，克荷維籓之寄；

translations.literal: With mountains as whetstone and rivers as girdle, you can bear the charge of maintaining the feudatory;
translations.idiomatic: With mountains as whetstone and rivers as girdle, you can bear the charge of the feudatory;

sentences.zh: 制節謹度，無忘執玉之心。

translations.literal: Observe measure and hold to regulation—do not forget the heart of one who bears jade as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: observe measure and hold to regulation—do not forget the heart of one who bears jade tribute.

sentences.zh: 念爾悃忱，朕甚嘉尚。

translations.literal: Considering your sincere devotion, I greatly commend it.
translations.idiomatic: Considering your sincere devotion, I greatly commend it.

sentences.zh: 今封爾為暹羅國王，錫之誥命，爾其益矢忠貞，廣宣聲教，膺茲榮寵，輯乃封圻。

translations.literal: Now I invest you as King of Siam and grant this patent; you must further devote loyalty, broadly spread civilization, accept this glorious favor, and keep your domain in order.
translations.idiomatic: Now I invest you as King of Siam and grant this patent; devote yourself further to loyalty, spread civilization, accept this honor, and keep your realm in order.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 保民社而王，纂休聲於舊服；

translations.literal: Protect the people and land as king, continue good renown in your old domain;
translations.idiomatic: Protect the people and land as king, continue good renown in your old domain;

sentences.zh: 守共球之職，懋嘉績於侯封。

translations.literal: Keep the duty of the common sphere, strive for fine achievement in your marquisate.
translations.idiomatic: keep the duty of the common sphere, strive for fine achievement in your marquisate.

sentences.zh: 欽哉，無替朕命！」

translations.literal: Revere this—do not neglect my command!"
translations.idiomatic: Revere this—do not neglect my command!"

sentences.zh: 二十三年，王遣正使王大統、副使坤孛述列瓦提，齎金葉表入貢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the king dispatched chief envoy Wang Datong and deputy envoy Kun Bo Su Lie Wa Ti, bearing a gold-leaf memorial to present tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three the king sent chief envoy Wang Datong and deputy Kun Bo Su Lie Wa Ti with a gold-leaf tribute memorial.

sentences.zh: 帝諭暹羅進貢員役，有不能乘馬者，官給夫轎，從人給舁夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor instructed that for Siam's tribute personnel, those unable to ride horses were to be given official sedan chairs, and attendants were to be given bearers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered sedan chairs for tribute personnel who could not ride, and bearers for attendants.

sentences.zh: 先是貢船抵虎跳門，守臣查驗後，進泊河干，封貯貨物，俟禮部文到，方准貿易。

translations.literal: Previously when tribute ships reached Hujiao Gate, the frontier official inspected them and then they moored at the river bank; goods were sealed and stored, and only when documents from the Board of Rites arrived was trade permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Previously tribute ships at Hujiao Gate were inspected, moored, and sealed until Board of Rites documents arrived before trade was allowed.

sentences.zh: 至是疏請嗣後貢船到廣，具報即准貿易，並請本國採買器用，乞諭地方官給照置辦，允之。

translations.literal: At this time a memorial requested that hereafter when tribute ships reached Guangdong, trade be permitted upon report; also requesting that purchases of utensils in China be licensed by local officials—this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial now asked that tribute ships at Guangdong trade upon report, and that local officials license purchases of Chinese goods—granted.

sentences.zh: 頒賞暹羅之鞾，始折絹。

translations.literal: Boots bestowed on Siam were first converted to silk.
translations.idiomatic: Boots bestowed on Siam were first commuted to silk.

sentences.zh: 貢使回國，禮部派司官、筆帖式各一人伴送。

translations.literal: When tribute envoys returned home, the Board of Rites dispatched one department official and one clerk each to escort them.
translations.idiomatic: Returning envoys were escorted by one Board of Rites department official and one clerk each.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，議定暹羅國王原賞緞三十四，今加十六，共表裏五十。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year it was decided that the King of Siam's original grant of thirty-four bolts of satin would now be increased by sixteen, totaling fifty for outer and inner garments.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-four Siam's satin grant was raised from thirty-four to fifty bolts for outer and inner garments.

sentences.zh: 四十七年，貢馴象二、金絲猴二。

translations.literal: In the forty-seventh year, they presented two trained elephants and two golden monkeys.
translations.idiomatic: In year forty-seven they sent two trained elephants and two golden langurs.

sentences.zh: 是年，禮官議准暹羅貢船壓艙貨物在廣東貿易，免其徵稅。

translations.literal: That year, ritual officials deliberated and approved that ballast cargo on Siam's tribute ships trading in Guangdong be exempt from taxation.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Board of Rites approved tax exemption for surplus cargo on Siam's tribute ships trading in Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 六十一年，部議暹羅入貢照安南國例，加賜國王緞八、紗四、羅八、織金紗羅各二；

translations.literal: In the sixty-first year, the ministry deliberated that Siam's tribute presentation follow the Annam precedent, adding for the king eight bolts of satin, four of gauze, eight of gauze weave, and two each of gold-woven gauze and gauze weave;
translations.idiomatic: In year sixty-one the ministry ruled that Siam's tribute grants follow Annam's precedent: for the king, eight bolts of satin, four of gauze, eight of plain gauze, and two each of gold-woven gauze and gauze.

sentences.zh: 王妃緞、織金緞、紗、織金紗、羅、織金羅各二。

translations.literal: For the queen consort, two each of satin, gold-woven satin, gauze, gold-woven gauze, gauze weave, and gold-woven gauze weave.
translations.idiomatic: The queen consort received two bolts each of satin, gold-woven satin, gauze, gold-woven gauze, plain gauze, and gold-woven gauze.

sentences.zh: 是年，國王奏稱彼國有紅皮船二，前被留禁，請令廣東督撫交貢使帶回。

translations.literal: That year the king memorialized that his country had two red-skinned ships previously detained, requesting that the Guangdong governor-general and provincial governor return them to the tribute envoys to bring back.
translations.idiomatic: That year the king reported two teak ships previously detained and asked the Guangdong governor and governor-general to return them to his envoys.

sentences.zh: 帝可其請，並諭禮部曰：「暹羅米甚豐足，若運米赴福建、廣東、寧波三處各十萬石貿易，有裨地方，免其稅。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted the request and also instructed the Board of Rites: "Siam's rice is very abundant; if rice is shipped to Fujian, Guangdong, and Ningbo, one hundred thousand shi each for trade, benefiting the regions, exempt it from tax.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor granted the request and told the Board of Rites: "Siam's rice is plentiful—if it ships one hundred thousand shi each to Fujian, Guangdong, and Ningbo for trade, benefiting those regions, exempt it from tax.

sentences.zh: 部臣與暹羅使臣議定，年運三十萬石，逾額米糧與貨物照例收稅。

translations.literal: Ministry officials negotiated with Siam's envoys and fixed annual shipment at three hundred thousand shi; grain and goods beyond the quota would be taxed according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Officials and Siamese envoys agreed on three hundred thousand shi annually; rice and goods beyond quota would be taxed as usual.

sentences.zh: 雍正二年十月，廣東巡撫年希堯陳暹羅運米並進方物，詔曰：「暹羅不憚險遠，進獻穀種、果樹及洋鹿、獵犬等物，恭順可嘉。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the second year of Yongzheng, Guangdong provincial governor Nian Xiyao reported Siam's rice shipments and presentation of local products; an edict said: "Siam, undaunted by peril and distance, presented grain seed, fruit trees, and foreign deer, hunting dogs, and other items—reverent submission worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Yongzheng 2 (1724), Governor Nian Xiyao reported Siam's rice and tribute goods; the court replied: "Undaunted by distance, Siam has sent grain seed, fruit trees, foreign deer, hunting dogs, and more—such reverence deserves praise.

sentences.zh: 壓船貨物概免徵稅，用獎輸心向化之誠。」

translations.literal: Ballast cargo on ships is entirely exempt from tax, to reward the sincerity of turning toward civilization."
translations.idiomatic: All surplus ship cargo is tax-free, to reward their sincere turn toward civilization."

sentences.zh: 六年，帝諭暹羅商船運來米穀永遠免稅。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Emperor instructed that rice and grain brought by Siam's merchant ships be permanently exempt from tax.
translations.idiomatic: In year six the Emperor permanently exempted rice shipped by Siamese merchant vessels from tax.

sentences.zh: 七年，常貢內有速香、安息香、袈裟、布疋等，帝以無必須之物，免其入貢，著為例。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, among regular tribute items were aloeswood, benzoin, kasaya robes, and bolts of cloth; the Emperor, deeming them unnecessary, exempted them from tribute and made this precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven regular tribute included aloeswood, benzoin, kasaya robes, and cloth; the Emperor waived these unnecessary items and made it precedent.

sentences.zh: 時貢使呈稱「京師為萬國景仰，國王欲令觀光上國，遍覽名勝，歸國陳述，以廣見聞」。

translations.literal: At the time the tribute envoy submitted: "The capital is admired by all nations; the king wishes to have them see the sights of the superior state, tour famous places, and on returning home relate what they saw to broaden knowledge."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy reported: "The capital is admired by all nations; the king wishes his men to tour the sights, visit famous places, and report home to broaden their knowledge."

sentences.zh: 帝命賢能司官帶領遊覽，並賞銀一千兩，遇所喜物購買。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered capable department officials to lead them on tours, and also bestowed one thousand taels of silver for purchases of items they liked.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor assigned capable officials to guide their tour and granted one thousand taels for purchases they fancied.

sentences.zh: 使臣復稱本國產馬甚小，國王命購數匹帶歸，允之，命馬價向內庫支給。

translations.literal: The envoys further said their country produced very small horses; the king had ordered them to purchase several to bring back—this was granted, with horse prices to be paid from the privy purse.
translations.idiomatic: The envoys said Siamese horses were small and the king wanted several purchased; the Emperor agreed and ordered payment from the privy purse.

sentences.zh: 復賜國王御書「天南樂國」扁額、緞二十五、玉器八、琺琅器一、松花石硯二、玻璃器二、瓷器十四。

translations.literal: Further bestowed on the king an imperial inscription plaque reading "Joyful Kingdom at Heaven's South," twenty-five bolts of satin, eight jade items, one cloisonné piece, two Songhua inkstones, two glass items, and fourteen pieces of porcelain.
translations.idiomatic: He also granted the king an imperial plaque reading "Joyful Kingdom at Heaven's South," twenty-five bolts of satin, eight jade pieces, one cloisonné vessel, two Songhua inkstones, two glass items, and fourteen porcelains.

sentences.zh: 貢使赴廣採買京弓、銅線等物，復詔賞給。

translations.literal: Tribute envoys went to Guangdong to purchase capital bows, copper wire, and other items—the Emperor again ordered rewards granted.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys purchased capital bows and copper wire in Guangdong, and the Emperor again ordered rewards.

sentences.zh: 乾隆元年六月，國王遣陪臣朗三立哇提等齎表及方物來貢，增馴象一隻，金緞二疋、花幔一條，並言昔賜蟒龍袍藏承恩亭上，曆世久遠，難保無虞，懇再賜一二襲。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Qianlong, the king dispatched attendant ministers Lang Sanli Wati and others bearing a memorial and local products in tribute, adding one trained elephant, two bolts of gold brocade, and one floral canopy, also stating that python-dragon robes previously bestowed were kept at Chengen Pavilion; over many generations it was hard to guarantee their safety, and they humbly requested one or two sets be granted again.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Qianlong 1 (1736), the king sent ministers Lang Sanli Wati and others with tribute, adding one trained elephant, two bolts of gold brocade, and a floral canopy; they said python-dragon robes kept at Chengen Pavilion were aging and asked for one or two fresh sets.

sentences.zh: 帝特賞蟒緞四疋。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially granted four bolts of python-pattern satin.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor specially granted four bolts of python-pattern satin.

sentences.zh: 禮部奏暹羅照丕雅大庫呈稱伊國造福送寺需銅，懇弛禁，議弗許，帝特賞八百斤。

translations.literal: The Board of Rites reported that Siam, through Zhao Piya Daku, stated their country needed copper for temple merit-making, humbly requesting relaxation of the ban; deliberation did not permit it, but the Emperor specially granted eight hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Board reported Siam, via Zhao Piya Daku, requested copper for temple offerings—the ministry refused, but the Emperor granted eight hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 八年，詔暹羅商人運米來閩、粵諸省貿易，萬石以上免船貨稅銀十之五，五千石以上免十之三。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, an edict stated that when Siam's merchants shipped rice to Fujian, Guangdong, and other provinces for trade, shipments above ten thousand shi exempted five-tenths of ship-cargo tax silver, above five thousand shi three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight Siamese rice merchants trading in Fujian and Guangdong received five-tenths tax relief above ten thousand shi and three-tenths above five thousand.

sentences.zh: 其米照市價公平發糶。

translations.literal: The rice was to be sold at fair market prices.
translations.idiomatic: Rice was to be sold at fair market prices.

sentences.zh: 若民間米多，官為收買，以補常平社倉，或散給沿海標營兵糧之用。

translations.literal: If civilian rice was plentiful, officials would purchase it to replenish Ever-Normal and Community Granaries, or distribute it for coastal garrison troop rations.
translations.idiomatic: If local supply was ample, officials would buy rice for granaries or coastal garrison rations.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入貢方物外，附黑熊一、鬥雞十二、太和雞十六、金絲白肚猿一。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, beyond tribute products, they additionally sent one black bear, twelve fighting cocks, sixteen Taihe chickens, and one golden white-bellied ape.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen they added one black bear, twelve fighting cocks, sixteen Taihe chickens, and one golden white-bellied langur.

sentences.zh: 十四年，國王遣陪臣朗呵派提等入貢，錫御書「炎服屏籓」四字。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, the king dispatched attendant ministers Lang Hepaiti and others in tribute; conferred imperial calligraphy of four characters: "Hot-Clime Screen and Rampart."
translations.idiomatic: In year fourteen attendant ministers Lang Hepaiti and others came in tribute; the Emperor granted the inscription "Hot-Clime Screen and Rampart."

sentences.zh: 十六年，帝諭閩督喀爾吉善等籌辦官運暹羅米法。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the Emperor instructed Fujian governor Ka'erjishan and others to plan official transport of Siam rice.
translations.idiomatic: In year sixteen the Emperor ordered the Fujian governor to plan official Siamese rice shipments.

sentences.zh: 疏陳非便，並言不如獎勵商人赴暹羅運米至二千石以上者，予議敘給頂戴，從之。

translations.literal: A memorial stated this was impractical and said it would be better to encourage merchants going to Siam to ship rice above two thousand shi, granting them ranked honors and official caps—this was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: A memorial called official transport impractical and proposed rewarding merchants who shipped over two thousand shi from Siam with honors and caps—approved.

sentences.zh: 十八年，國王遣使入貢，懇賜人葠、纓牛、良馬、象牙、及通徹規儀內監。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, the king dispatched envoys in tribute, humbly requesting ginseng, yaks, fine horses, ivory, and eunuchs thoroughly versed in court protocol.
translations.idiomatic: In year eighteen the king's envoys requested ginseng, yaks, fine horses, ivory, and protocol-savvy eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 禮臣不可，帝加賜人葠四斤，特飭使臣歸國曉諭國王「恪守規制，益勵敬恭」。

translations.literal: Ritual officials refused; the Emperor added four jin of ginseng and specially ordered the envoys returning home to instruct the king: "Strictly observe regulations and further encourage reverence."
translations.idiomatic: Officials refused; the Emperor added four jin of ginseng and told envoys to instruct the king to "observe regulations and stay reverent."

sentences.zh: 二十二年，入貢，特賜其王蟒緞、錦緞各二，閃緞、片金緞各一，絲緞四，玉器、瑪瑙各一，松花石硯二，琺琅器十有三，瓷器百有四。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, on presenting tribute, specially granted the king two each of python satin and brocade satin, one each of shimmering satin and leaf-gold satin, four silk satins, one jade and one agate item each, two Songhua inkstones, thirteen cloisonné pieces, and one hundred four porcelains.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-two the king received two python and two brocade satins, one shimmering and one leaf-gold satin, four silk satins, jade and agate, two Songhua inkstones, thirteen cloisonné pieces, and 104 porcelains.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，暹羅入貢，賜與前同。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, Siam presented tribute; grants were the same as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty-one Siam's tribute grants matched the previous ones.

sentences.zh: 頃之，兩廣總督李侍堯奏暹羅為花肚番所破，繳還原頒賜物。

translations.literal: Shortly after, Liangguang governor-general Li Shiyao memorialized that Siam had been destroyed by the Huadufen and returned the originally bestowed gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, Governor-General Li Shiyao reported Siam destroyed by the Huadufen and returned prior imperial gifts.

sentences.zh: 花肚番即緬甸也。

translations.literal: The Huadufen were Burma.
translations.idiomatic: The Huadufen were the Burmese.

sentences.zh: 當其時，緬甸攻暹羅，進圍其國都阿由提亞，三月陷之，殺其王，暹羅遂亡。

translations.literal: At that time Burma attacked Siam, advanced to besiege its capital Ayutthaya, captured it in the third month, killed its king, and Siam perished.
translations.idiomatic: Burma besieged Ayutthaya, took it in the third month, killed the king, and Siam fell.

sentences.zh: 緬甸酋懵駁既破暹羅，恃強侵雲南邊，高宗疊遣將軍明瑞、大學士傅恆、將軍阿桂、阿裏袞等征之，緬甸調征暹羅軍自救。

translations.literal: After Burmese chief Mengbo destroyed Siam, relying on strength he encroached on Yunnan's border; the Gaozong repeatedly dispatched General Mingrui, Grand Secretary Fu Heng, Generals Agui and Aligun and others to campaign; Burma recalled troops from Siam for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Mengbo destroyed Siam he encroached on Yunnan; the Gaozong sent Mingrui, Fu Heng, Agui, and Aligun against him; Burma recalled its Siamese garrison.

sentences.zh: 阿由提亞之陷也，暹羅守長鄭昭方率軍有事柬埔寨，聞都城陷，旋師赴援，疊與緬甸戰，構兵數年。

translations.literal: When Ayutthaya fell, Siam's frontier commander Zheng Zhao was leading troops against Cambodia; hearing the capital had fallen, he turned his army to aid, repeatedly fought Burma, and was at war for years.
translations.idiomatic: When Ayutthaya fell, frontier commander Zheng Zhao was campaigning in Cambodia; he turned back, fought Burma repeatedly for years.

sentences.zh: 既以緬甸困于中國，鄭昭乘其疲敝擊破之，國復。

translations.literal: Since Burma was strained by China, Zheng Zhao seized their exhaustion to defeat them and the kingdom was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Strained by war with China, Burma weakened; Zheng Zhao routed them and restored the kingdom.

sentences.zh: 昭，中國廣東人也。

translations.literal: Zhao was a man of Guangdong in China.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was a native of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 父賈于暹羅，生昭。

translations.literal: His father traded in Siam; Zhao was born there.
translations.idiomatic: His father traded in Siam, where Zhao was born.

sentences.zh: 長有才略，仕暹羅。

translations.literal: Growing up talented and resourceful, he served Siam.
translations.idiomatic: Talented and capable, he entered Siamese service.

sentences.zh: 既破緬軍，國人推昭為主，遷都盤穀，鎮撫綏輯，國日殷富。

translations.literal: After defeating the Burmese army, the people acclaimed Zhao as ruler, moved the capital to Bangkok, pacified and settled the realm, and the country grew daily richer.
